# Intake Draft — Add per-shortcut option to control whether a shortcut opens a command pane (WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL)

## Problem statement

Every chord shortcut in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` unconditionally opens a pane when dispatched: shell commands (`!!`/`!`) open a visible "Command Output" herdr pane via `run-in-pane.sh`, and agent commands (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:`) open a pi agent pane via `send-to-pi.sh`. There is no way to configure a shortcut to execute without opening a pane — high-frequency, low-feedback actions (e.g. `a-y` audit approve) force the user to dismiss a pane on every use.

## Users

- **Herdr worklist users** who drive Worklog workflows via chord shortcuts and want quiet, non-intrusive execution for actions that need no visual confirmation (approve, priority changes, etc.).
- **Producers / reviewers** using `a-y` (audit approve) repeatedly across many `in_review` items.

### User stories

- As a user, when I press a shortcut configured with `open_pane: false`, I want the command to run in the background (no pane opens) so I can keep working uninterrupted — and I want its output written to a log file so I can inspect what happened later.
- As a user, when I press any other shortcut, I want the pane to open exactly as it does today (default behavior unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Schema** — `ShortcutEntry` in `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` gains an optional `openPane` boolean, parsed from the `open_pane` key in shortcuts.json. Missing/invalid values default to opening a pane (backward compatible; invalid values are logged and treated as omitted, mirroring the `code_freeze` pattern).
2. **Dispatch — shell commands** — A `!!`/`!` shortcut with `open_pane: false` executes its command in the background (no herdr pane created) with stdout/stderr captured to a log file for later inspection.
3. **Dispatch — agent commands** — An agent shortcut (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:`) with `open_pane: false` runs headless (no pi agent pane created), honoring the entry's `model`, with output captured to a log file. The work-item ↔ pane association (WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9) is skipped when no pane is created.
4. **Default unchanged** — Shortcuts without `open_pane` (all current entries) behave exactly as today: shell commands open a visible command-output pane; agent commands open a pi agent pane.
5. **Test case applied** — The `a-y` (audit approve) entry in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` is set to `open_pane: false`; pressing `a-y` approves the item without opening a pane, and the worklist refresh shows the updated state.
6. **All related documentation is updated** — `packages/herdr/README.md` (shortcut schema section, alongside `model` and `code_freeze`) documents the new `open_pane` field and its semantics.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes, including new unit tests for parsing/validation and dispatch routing (shell + agent, pane vs. no-pane, log-file creation).

## Constraints

- Follow the established optional-field pattern in `shortcut-config.ts` (`model`, `code_freeze`): snake_case JSON key → camelCase TS field, invalid values never break or hide a shortcut.
- Background execution must be detached and non-blocking — the TUI event loop and process lifecycle must be unaffected (mirror the existing `spawn(..., { detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' })` + `child.unref()` pattern in `index.ts`).
- No behavior change for entries without `open_pane` (default = open pane).
- Log file location is an implementation decision; a sensible default is a per-run file under a known directory (e.g. the OS tmpdir or `<worklog-root>`), with the path recorded/logged so it can be located for inspection.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — 22 entries; `a-y` is `["a","y"]` → `!!wl reviewed <id> false && wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close yes --summary 'Approved by manual review'` (view `both`, stages `in_review`).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `ShortcutEntry` interface (command, view, chord, label?, description?, stages?, model?, codeFreeze?) + `parseShortcutEntry` validation + `ShortcutRegistry`; optional fields follow snake_case→camelCase parsing with invalid-value logging.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `onCommand(command, model)` routes: `agent` → `send-to-pi.sh` (pi pane, claims item, optional pane-id capture); `pane` (`!!`/`!`) → `run-in-pane.sh` (visible Command Output pane); `stdout` → `CMD:` prefix fallback.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `processChordInput` resolves chords and stores `resolvedCommand` / `resolvedModel` on `ChordState`; `resolveAndRouteCommand` calls `onCommand(resolvedCommand, model)`.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — splits a pane right, runs the command in a shell wrapper, keeps the pane open for inspection.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — opens a pi agent pane with the command as initial prompt; `--model` / `--pane-id-file` options exist.
- Headless pi execution (`pi -p --mode json`) is an established pattern elsewhere (e.g. `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`).

## Desired change

- Add `open_pane: false` support to the shortcut schema, plumbed through `parseShortcutEntry` → `ChordState` → `onCommand`, defaulting to open-pane behavior.
- In `index.ts` dispatch: when a shortcut entry has `openPane: false`, spawn the shell command (or headless pi for agent commands) detached with output redirected to a log file instead of opening a pane; skip pane-id capture for agent commands; keep the worklist refresh cycle so results become visible.
- Set `a-y` to `open_pane: false` in `shortcuts.json` as the proof/test case.
- Document the field in `packages/herdr/README.md`; add unit tests for parsing and dispatch.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — Add `openPane?: boolean` to `ShortcutEntry`; parse/validate `open_pane` in `parseShortcutEntry` (default true, invalid → logged + omitted).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Set `"open_pane": false` on the `a-y` (audit approve) entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Plumb resolved `openPane` through `ChordState` (`resolvedOpenPane`) and `onCommand` signature (`command, model, openPane`).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Branch dispatch on `openPane`: background execution with log-file redirect (shell: `bash -c` detached; agent: headless `pi -p --mode json` honoring `model`) vs. current pane-opening paths; skip pane-id capture when no pane opens.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — Parsing tests: `open_pane: true/false/omitted/invalid`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (or worklist tests) — Dispatch routing tests: no-pane shell + agent, log file written, default still opens panes.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Document the `open_pane` field alongside `model` / `code_freeze` (schema table + behavior notes).

## Related work

- WL-0MS95CEAE0080EB4 — *a-y (audit approve) shortcut does nothing — should run wl command visibly in a herdr pane* (completed): introduced the visible-pane execution for `!!` commands that this feature now makes optional.
- WL-0MS7MFILJ0079283 — *Visible command execution pane for !/!! prefixed commands* (completed): created `run-in-pane.sh`; success/failure pane lifecycle.
- WL-0MS9HIUE0002JAKQ — *Leave command-output pane open after successful !/!! command so output is inspectable* (completed): pane stays open for inspection — the exact behavior `open_pane: false` lets users opt out of.
- WL-0MSD48ZFC0043AO3 — *Add model to the shortcut keys* (completed): established the optional-field schema + `onCommand(command, model)` plumbing pattern this feature extends.
- WL-0MSD81VEL009XHWA — *code_freeze field* (referenced in shortcut-config.ts): the invalid-value→omit precedent.
- WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9 — *Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item* (in progress): pane-id capture to skip when no pane is created.
- WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7 — *Evaluate Pi subprocess mechanisms: headless pi -p vs herdr pane* (completed): established headless `pi -p --mode json` as a valid non-pane execution mechanism.
- WL-0MSHIA53D009DJOT — *Keep focus on the Herdr selection list when a shortcut command creates a pane* (open, medium): complementary UX concern for pane-opening shortcuts; related but not blocking.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (low):** Log files accumulate — mitigate by using a per-run filename (timestamp) under a single directory and documenting the location; cleanup is out of scope.
- **Risk (medium):** Headless agent execution (`pi -p --mode json`) may not behave identically to interactive pane execution for all workflows (e.g. `/skill:implement` spawning its own panes, long-running interactive steps). Mitigation: default remains pane-opening; `open_pane: false` is opt-in per shortcut; the a-y test case exercises only a shell command.
- **Assumption:** "Command pane" scope includes both the visible command-output pane (shell commands) and the pi agent pane (agent commands) — confirmed by user (Q2: "all").
- **Assumption:** Background execution must still produce an inspectable record — log file per user (Q1: option b).
- **Scope-creep guard:** Worklist auto-refresh timing, log rotation, and a settings-level default are out of scope; record as separate work items if needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When a shortcut is set to NOT open a pane, how should the command execute?" — Answer (rgardler): option **b — run in the background but write output to a log file for later inspection**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Should the flag apply only to shell commands (`!!`/`!` → command-output pane), or also to agent commands (`/skill:*`, `/intake` → pi agent pane)?" — Answer (rgardler): **all** shortcut types. Source: interactive reply.

## Problem

In the herdr worklog-selection-list plugin, every fetch used by the auto-refresh cycle spawns `wl` via execFile WITHOUT a timeout: `runWl(args)` (fetcher.ts:376) passes `timeout` to execFileAsync only when `timeoutMs !== undefined` (:356), and no caller in the refresh path supplies one (fetchNextItems, fetchItemsByStage, fetchMandatorySubsets, fetchActionableCount). `doRefresh` awaits these inside a `refreshInFlight` single-flight guard (worklist.ts:2497-2503); if a spawn hangs (e.g. waiting on the worklog lock during a long `wl sync`, or a stuck child), the guard stays true forever and EVERY subsequent refresh is skipped — the pane freezes even while focused, with no error surfaced.

Note: runSync (auto-sync.ts:226) already has a 60s spawn safety timeout; the refresh read path does not.

related-to: WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9 (same bug class in the downtime worker path — getNextItem/getNextAuditCandidate in index.ts use direct execFileAsync with no timeout; a single fix adding bounded timeouts to ALL wl spawns would close both).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every wl spawn in the refresh/sync fetch path has a bounded timeout (recommend 30-60s, configurable or aligned with existing constants).
- [ ] A timed-out refresh fails gracefully: toast (`Refresh failed`), guard cleared, next tick retries — never a permanently wedged refreshInFlight.
- [ ] Unit tests: hung execFile resolves to failure after the timeout and the next refresh tick proceeds.

## Suggested approach

Pass a default timeoutMs inside runWl (or runWlInner) when the caller omits one, e.g. `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000`, keeping the option to override. Verify no existing tests depend on unbounded spawns.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSB445R1004PM3I** – Impl: idle-gated auto-refresh/auto-sync in browse widget (browse.ts) (completed)

1. **Tests: hung wl refresh resolves via timeout; next tick proceeds** — `WL-0MT60Q89I003KRMJ` (task, test-first). # Intake Brief — Herdr: filter by priority via f-p-* chords, stage filters become f-s-* (WL-0MSKC8T46006999S) ## Headline Add priority filtering to the Herdr worklist, complementing the existing stage filter: the filter chord gains an axis key — stage filters become `f s ` and new priority filters are `f p ` — with a single active filter (replace semantics), a typed `/wl --priority

` command for parity, and sprint clearing all filters. ## Problem Statement The Herdr worklist currently filters only by stage via single-key chords (`f i`, `f n`, `f p`, `f r`, `f s`). Producers and agents frequently want to see everything at a given priority (e.g. all `critical` items) regardless of stage, which is not possible today. The filter chord needs an axis dimension: `f `. Re-using the existing single-key chords would collide (`f p` currently means "filter plan"), so stage filters move under `f s *` and priority filters take `f p *`. ## Users - Herdr plugin users (producers, developers, agents) who browse the worklist inside a Herdr pane. ### Example User Stories - As a producer, I want to press `f p c` to see every open critical item so I can prioritise review, regardless of stage. - As a developer, I want to type `/wl --priority high` to see all open high-priority work when deciding what to pick up next. - As an agent, I want `f s i` to keep filtering idea-stage items with the same keystroke muscle memory I had for `f i`. ## Acceptance Criteria 1. New priority filter chords work: `f p c` (critical), `f p h` (high), `f p m` (medium), `f p l` (low) filter the worklist to items of that priority. 2. Stage filter chords are remapped under the stage axis: `f s i` (idea), `f s n` (intake), `f s p` (plan), `f s r` (review) filter by stage; the old single-key stage chords (`f i`, `f n`, `f p`, `f r`) no longer trigger filters, and `f s` alone no longer resolves to a command (it is a chord prefix only). 3. Replace semantics (single filter slot): applying a priority filter clears any active stage filter, and vice versa; the list header shows which filter is active. 4. Sprint clears all filters: `f s s` and `/wl` (no arguments) restore the default unfiltered view, clearing both stage and priority filters; a priority-axis clear exists (proposed `f p s`) that returns to the unfiltered view. 5. Typed parity command: `/wl --priority ` filters by priority, accepting canonical names `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`; invalid/unknown priority values fall back gracefully (no crash, no filter change), matching the current `/wl ` behaviour. 6. Priority-filtered views follow the same semantics as stage-filtered views: every open root item with that priority (`wl list --status open --priority

--root-only`) — no `browseItemCount` cap, no `wl next` selection omission, children hidden and reachable via expand, standard sortIndex order. 7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, with new unit tests covering chord registration, dispatch, replace semantics, and the priority fetcher. 8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (Herdr README filter sections, code comments). ## Constraints - **Scope is the Herdr plugin** (`packages/herdr/`): `shortcuts.json`, `worklist.ts`, `fetcher.ts`, tests, and README. The Pi TUI extension and the `wl` CLI are out of scope (the CLI already supports `--priority`). - **No new settings or configuration flags.** The chord scheme and `/wl --priority` command are the only interfaces. - **Single active filter.** Stage and priority filters are mutually exclusive (user decision: replace, not combine). - Keep the existing stage-filter fetch semantics (open, root-only, uncapped, sortIndex order) — the priority filter mirrors them. ## Existing State - Filter chords in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`: `f i` → `/wl idea`, `f n` → `/wl intake`, `f p` → `/wl plan`, `f r` → `/wl review`, `f s` → `/wl` (sprint, unfiltered). - `dispatchChordCommand` in `worklist.ts` maps `/wl ` (via `STAGE_MAP`) to `state.applyFilter(stage)` and `/wl` (no args) to `state.clearFilter()`; `isWlViewCommand` triggers a refetch after a filter dispatch (WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G). - `WorkItemListState.activeFilter` holds the single stage filter; `_applyFilters()` filters `item.stage === activeFilter`; the header renders `(filtered: )`. - `fetchItemsForView(activeFilter, defaultFetcher)` → `fetchItemsByStage(stage)` → `wl list --status open --stage --root-only` (fetcher.ts). - `wl list` natively supports `--priority` (already used by `fetchMandatorySubsets` for the critical subset). - A legacy digit-based filter mode (`state.mode === 'filter'`, `formatFilterPrompt`) exists but is unreachable from the keyboard since the `/` prompt was removed — out of scope unless trivially affected. ## Desired Change 1. **`shortcuts.json`** — Remove the `f i`/`f n`/`f p`/`f r` stage chords and the single `f s` sprint chord. Add stage-axis chords `f s i|n|p|r` (→ `/wl idea|intake|plan|review`) and `f s s` (→ `/wl` sprint, clears all filters). Add priority-axis chords `f p l|m|h|c` (→ `/wl --priority low|medium|high|critical`) and `f p s` (→ `/wl`, clear-priority, returns to unfiltered). 2. **`worklist.ts`** — Add a priority filter slot to `WorkItemListState` with replace semantics (`applyFilter` clears priority; new `applyPriorityFilter` clears stage; `clearFilter` clears both). Extend `_applyFilters` to match stage OR priority. Extend `dispatchChordCommand` and `isWlViewCommand` to handle `/wl --priority

`. Update the header filter label to show the active axis+value. `fetchItemsForView` routes priority filters to the new fetcher. 3. **`fetcher.ts`** — Add `fetchItemsByPriority(priority)` running `wl list --status open --priority

--root-only`, mirroring `fetchItemsByStage`. 4. **Tests** — Update `shortcut-config.test.ts` (chord registration: `f s *`, `f p *`, removal of old single-key chords) and `worklist.test.ts` (dispatch of `/wl --priority

`, replace semantics, clear-all sprint, header label); add `fetchItemsByPriority` coverage in the fetcher tests. 5. **README** — Update the filter-by-stage chord documentation to the `f s *` scheme and document `f p *` priority filters and `/wl --priority

`. ## Key Files (predicted) - `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Replace the single-key stage chords with `f s *` stage chords and add `f p *` priority chords. - `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Priority filter slot with replace semantics, `/wl --priority` dispatch, header label, `isWlViewCommand` update. - `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — New `fetchItemsByPriority` mirroring `fetchItemsByStage`. - `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Dispatch, replace-semantics, clear-all, and header tests. - `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — Chord registration tests for the new `f s *` / `f p *` scheme. - `tests/herdr/fetcher.test.ts` — `fetchItemsByPriority` mocked-socket tests. - `packages/herdr/README.md` — Filter documentation updates. ## Related Work - **WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G** (in-progress) — "When filtering by stage, show all open work items in that stage": established the stage-filter fetch semantics (open, root-only, uncapped) and `/wl ` dispatch that this work extends to priorities. - **WL-0MSGSE15000746F7** — sprint `/wl` chord returning to the default view; the `f s` chord being remapped here. - **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** — root-only top-level lists; semantics reused by the priority filter. - **WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP** — Herdr work item selection list (origin of the plugin's list/filter UI). - **WL-0MSGTSPXK007POB1** — header shows the active filter; the header label changes here for priorities. ### Related work (automated report) Automated report from the find-related skill (full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MSKC8T46006999S.md`). Low relevance — flagged for traceability only: - **WL-0MSB19J56006E87J** – Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM) (completed) - **WL-0MQFB8N990056T8P** – [test-failure] tests/tui/controller-watch.test.ts > TuiController - Database Watch > always re-renders on watch refresh even when dataset appears unchanged (completed) - **WL-0MQF95NCC0024H61** – wl next Stage 3 blocker surfacing still returns child items (completed) ## Risks & Assumptions - **Chord conflict risk (medium):** `f p` changes meaning from "filter plan" to "priority axis leader". Mitigation: remove the old `f p` plan chord; `f p` alone must not resolve (registry prefix semantics already support this); tests assert the old chords no longer resolve. - **Muscle memory regression (low):** existing users of `f i`/`f n`/`f r` must learn `f s i`/`f s n`/`f s r`. Mitigation: README documents the new scheme; `f s` hints show in the chord help line. - **Assumption — priority clear chord:** the exact key for the priority-axis clear is proposed as `f p s` (symmetric with the stage sprint). Final key choice is a product detail; the brief records the proposal (user confirmed a priority-clear exists). - **Assumption — typed command syntax:** `/wl --priority ` mirrors the existing `/wl ` syntax; alternative syntaxes (e.g. `/wl priority:

`) are possible but the `--priority` form matches the `wl list` flag naming. - **Scope creep:** the legacy unreachable digit-based filter mode (`formatFilterPrompt`) is out of scope; any change to it should be a separate work item. ## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers - Q1: "Can a stage filter and a priority filter be active simultaneously (e.g., `f s i` then `f p c` → critical idea items), or does each new filter chord replace the previous one (single filter slot)?" — Answer (user): "replace". Source: interactive reply (this intake session). Final: single active filter; applying one axis clears the other. - Q2: "Should sprint clear *all* filters (stage + priority), and is a way to clear just the priority filter needed (e.g., a `f p` clear chord)?" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply (this intake session). Final: `f s s` and `/wl` clear all filters; a priority-axis clear chord exists (proposed `f p s`, equivalent to returning to the unfiltered view under replace semantics). - Q3: "Should the priority filter also be reachable via a typed command (e.g., `/wl --priority critical`) for parity with `/wl `, or is the chord-only approach sufficient?" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply (this intake session). Final: `/wl --priority ` is a supported typed command with graceful fallback for invalid values.

# Auto-revert in_review items to plan_complete when marked not ready to close

## Problem Statement

When a work item in the `in_review` stage (status `completed`) is marked "not ready to close" — via `wl update <id> --audit-text "Ready to close: No"` or `wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no` — nothing happens to the item's lifecycle state. The item remains `completed`/`in_review`, which signals to the heartbeat and release tooling that it is awaiting closure. An item whose audit says it is *not* ready to close should no longer be presented as awaiting closure; its stage should revert to `plan_complete` so it returns to the planning queue for further work.

## Users

- **Producers / reviewers** who audit an `in_review` item, find it lacking, and mark it "not ready to close".
  - *As a producer, I want an in_review item I mark as "not ready to close" to drop out of the ready-to-close queue automatically, so it isn't swept up by heartbeat/release tooling.*
- **Agents / automation** that run audits and write `Ready to close: No` verdicts.
  - *As an agent, I want the lifecycle state to stay consistent automatically when I mark an item not ready, so I don't have to remember to reset status/stage manually.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When `wl update <id> --audit-text "Ready to close: No"` is run on an item with stage `in_review` (status `completed`), the item is automatically reverted to status `open` / stage `plan_complete`.
2. When `wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no` is run on an item with stage `in_review` (status `completed`), the item is automatically reverted to status `open` / stage `plan_complete`.
3. The item's priority is unchanged by the reversion (priority is preserved, not reset).
4. No reversion occurs when the item is not in the `in_review`/`completed` state (e.g., `done` stage, or already `open`/`in-progress`), or when the audit verdict is "Ready to close: Yes" — behavior is otherwise unchanged.
5. The reversion is reported: JSON output includes the reverted item's `from`/`to` status and stage, and human-readable output prints a summary line (e.g. `[WL-XXX reverted from completed/in_review to open/plan_complete]`), following the reporting style of the priority-downgrade cascade.
6. Unit tests cover: reversion via `--audit-text`, reversion via `audit-set`, no-op on `done` items, no-op on non-in_review items, no-op on "Ready to close: Yes", and priority preservation.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The reversion must only fire on the "not ready to close" verdict (`Ready to close: No` / `--ready-to-close no`), not on any other audit text.
- The transition must respect `statusStageCompatibility`: `open` status already permits `plan_complete` stage, so the target state is valid per existing rules.
- The audit write must remain best-effort; if the reversion's `db.update` fails (e.g., file lock), the command should not crash — surface a warning (mirroring the sibling demotion item's best-effort guidance).
- The audit text write path must not be blocked by the existing "skip db.update() when no fields changed" safety guard in `update.ts` — the reversion is an intentional lifecycle consequence of the audit verdict, not an accidental field change.

## Existing State

- `wl update --audit-text` writes to the `audit_results` table via `db.saveAuditResult()` in `src/commands/update.ts` (~line 219–246); a safety guard skips `db.update()` when no work-item fields changed (~line 358).
- `wl audit-set` writes the audit result in `src/commands/audit-result.ts` (~line 154–165) without touching status/stage.
- The API-level audit write path in `src/api.ts` (`normalizeUpdateInputWithAudit`, `writeAuditResult`) also persists audit results without lifecycle changes.
- `statusStageCompatibility` in `config.defaults.yaml`: `open: [idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_progress]` — `open`/`plan_complete` is a valid combination.
- Sibling item WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6 implements the same demotion pattern (`completed`/`in_review` → `open`/`plan_complete`) triggered by adding a child — same target state, different trigger, and shares the reporting convention.

## Desired Change

Implement the reversion as a shared helper (e.g., `revertToPlanComplete(item, db)` or similar) called after an audit write whenever the verdict is not-ready-to-close and the item's stage is `in_review` / status `completed`:

1. **`src/commands/update.ts`** — after a successful `db.saveAuditResult` when the parsed verdict is `Ready to close: No`, check the item state and revert if `in_review`/`completed`.
2. **`src/commands/audit-result.ts`** — in the `audit-set` action, after `db.saveAuditResult` when `--ready-to-close no`, apply the same reversion.
3. **`src/api.ts`** — decide whether the API audit write path (`writeAuditResult` / `normalizeUpdateInputWithAudit`) should also trigger the reversion for consistency; if yes, apply the same helper.
4. **Reporting** — extend JSON output with a `reverted` field (`{ from: { status, stage }, to: { status, stage } }`) and add a human summary line, following the priority-downgrade cascade style.
5. **Tests** — add unit/integration tests covering AC 1–6 (see `tests/cli/audit-results-cli.test.ts`, `tests/cli/audit.test.ts`, and any update-command test files).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--audit-text` write path; add reversion after not-ready verdict
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` — `wl audit-set` action; add reversion after `--ready-to-close no`
- `src/api.ts` — API-level audit write path; apply reversion for consistency (decision needed)
- `src/audit.ts` — audit parsing helpers (`inspectAuditFirstLine`, `buildAuditEntry`) already produce the ready-to-close verdict
- `src/persistent-store.ts` — `saveAuditResult` / `getAuditResult`; `update` for the reversion write
- `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` — document the reversion behavior
- `tests/cli/audit-results-cli.test.ts`, `tests/cli/audit.test.ts` — audit CLI test coverage

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6** ("Demote completed/in_review parent to plan_complete when a child is added", ContextHub, open/intake_complete) — implements the same `completed`/`in_review` → `open`/`plan_complete` demotion triggered by adding a child. This item is the mirror trigger (not-ready-to-close audit verdict). Shared helper and reporting convention; the two should not conflict.
- **WL-0MMS4EUMU15LEU7B** ("Audit Write Path (CLI/API)", ContextHub, completed) — established the audit write paths that this change hooks into.
- **WL-0MPZNK0UW009CI6C** ("Implementation: wl audit set subcommand", ContextHub, completed) — the `audit-set` command this change extends.
- **WL-0MRSGMTYU009OZCF** ("Add --audit-file to wl audit-set", ContextHub, completed) — related `audit-set` surface area.
- **WL-0MNFSCMDU0075BMH** ("Audit parser rejects valid 'Ready to close' audits; improve error message", ContextHub, completed) — the first-line audit parsing that determines the verdict.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: extending the reversion to the API path (`src/api.ts`) may surface API consumers that depend on audit writes not changing lifecycle state. Mitigation: if the API path proves risky, restrict reversion to the two CLI commands and record API consistency as a separate follow-up item.
- **Assumption**: "not ready to close" means exactly the audit verdict `Ready to close: No` (or `--ready-to-close no`); no other audit text triggers reversion.
- **Assumption**: reversion target is status `open` / stage `plan_complete` per user answers; priority is preserved (user answer: "the medium is for this item, for the items being reset the priority should remain unchanged").
- **Assumption**: reversion is reported in output (JSON field + human line), mirroring the priority-downgrade cascade and the sibling demotion item's reporting convention.
- **Risk**: the existing safety guard in `update.ts` ("skip db.update() when no fields changed") must be deliberately bypassed only for the intentional reversion — implement carefully to avoid accidental transitions on other audit texts.
- **Risk**: batch `wl update` over multiple ids where some are in_review will revert each qualifying item independently; must not break non-qualifying items in the same batch.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What triggers the "not ready to close" flag — a manual `wl update --stage plan_complete` action by the producer, or automated (heartbeat/audit system detecting issues)? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "wl update command".
- Q: What happens to the item's status? Should it remain `completed` (just the stage reverts), or go back to `in_progress`/`open` so work can resume? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "open".
- Q: Priority reset? The seed intent says `--priority medium` — should this override the item's current priority? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "No the medium is for this item, for the items being reset the priority should remain unchanged" → `medium` is the priority of THIS work item; reverted items keep their priority.
- Q: Where does the "not ready to close" trigger live — Option A (setting `--audit-text "Ready to close: No"` or `wl audit-set --ready-to-close no` on an in_review item automatically reverts) or Option B (new explicit flag/command)? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "A".
- Q: When the item reverts to `open`/`plan_complete`, should status also be `in_progress` (so an agent can claim and continue immediately), or leave it `open` so it must be formally claimed first? — Answer (user, interactive reply): status is `open`; the item must be formally claimed again (consistent with the sibling demotion item WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6).


---

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS6AAW3M004JK9U** – Reselect item after list reorder from status change (completed)
- **WL-0MS9HIUE0002JAKQ** – Leave command-output pane open after successful !/!! command so output is inspectable (completed)
- **WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW** – Herdr: in_review stage filter (f-r) shows 0 items because stage-filtered fetch restricts to status=open (open)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-auto-revert-in-review-not-ready-to-close-WL-0MSKHYI5U0069FVV.md` — matched: auto, close, complete, intent, item, items, marked, plan, ready, revert, review, seed, should, stage, when
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSDZ64J8005Q2JJ-grid-rebalance-python-tests-mocked-socke/CLI.md` — matched: auto, close, complete, item, items, marked, plan, ready, returned, review, should, stage, when
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA-wire-read-commands-through-cache-spawn-i/CLI.md` — matched: auto, close, complete, item, items, marked, plan, ready, returned, review, should, stage, when

## Summary

The shared test runner (skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py) defines a static NODE_SUITE_DIRS = (tests/node, tests/cli, tests/unit). ContextHub has no tests/node directory (git ls-files confirms it was never tracked), so the canonical full-suite command npm --silent test -- tests/node always exits 1 with 'No test files found'.

## Impact

The audit skill's automatic full-suite verification (SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W) queries the per-repo test cache for EVERY canonical suite command and requires exit code 0. The permanently-failing tests/node entry means the audit runner can NEVER inject automatic green-run evidence for ContextHub audits — execution-dependent acceptance criteria (e.g. 'Full project test suite passes') stay partial and block closure.

## Workaround used in release v1.0.9

Operator ran pytest (103 passed) + npx vitest run (4117 passed) at the release HEAD and passed --green-run HEAD to each audit — honest attestation, but manual.

## Suggested fix

Either (a) filter NODE_SUITE_DIRS by directory existence in the shared runner, or (b) make ContextHub's suite definition explicit. Discovered during release v1.0.9 remediation (discovered-from:WL-0MSG80FQ9000C8GE).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The canonical full-suite command set for ContextHub (as resolved by full_suite_commands()) matches the suites that actually exist in the repo.
- [ ] run_tests.py --summary --suite all reports green for every suite in the canonical set at a green HEAD.

# Intake Draft — Herdr selection list: collapsible group headings with item counts

**Work item:** WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94

## Problem statement

The Herdr work-item selection list renders group separators (`── Group 1 ──`, `── Idea ──`, `── In Review ──`) between items, but these heading rows are pure chrome: they carry no item count, they cannot be collapsed to hide a group's items, and up/down navigation skips over them entirely (the cursor can never land on a heading). With several groups on screen this wastes vertical space and gives the user no way to focus on one group.

## Users

- **Herdr plugin users** (operators running the work-item selection list pane).

User stories:
- "As a producer reviewing the worklist, I want each group heading to show how many items it contains, so I can see at a glance where the bulk of the work is."
- "As a producer, I want to collapse a group by pressing Tab while its heading is selected, so I can hide items I'm not interested in and focus on the rest."
- "As a producer, I want up/down navigation to land on heading rows, so I can reach them to collapse/expand them."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Each group heading row displays the label plus the number of items in that group (e.g. `── Group 1 (4) ──`). The count reflects the top-level items assigned to the group in the current view (post stage-filter), regardless of collapse state.
- AC2: Up/down navigation (j/k and arrow keys) moves the selection onto heading rows as well as items; headings are no longer skipped. Page up/down, first/last, and wrap-around behave consistently with the heading rows included.
- AC3: Pressing Tab while a heading row is selected toggles that group's collapse state: collapsed hides the group's items from both the render and navigation; expanded shows them. Tab on an item row keeps its existing expand/collapse-children behaviour unchanged.
- AC4: Collapsed-group state lives in memory for the session (like `expandedItems`), survives list refreshes, and does not persist across pane restarts.
- AC5: When a heading is selected, the metadata panel shows the group info (label + count) rather than stale item metadata; Enter on a heading is a no-op (only Tab toggles).
- AC6: The `rows - 1` line-count invariant, code-freeze banner, metadata-panel sizing, and stage-filter views keep working; full Herdr test suite (vitest for packages/herdr) passes.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant docs site entries.

## Constraints

- The change is confined to the Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr`) — the Pi TUI Worklog extension has its own browse implementation and is out of scope.
- `packages/herdr` has zero npm dependencies; the implementation must stay self-contained (the existing duplicated `grouping.ts` pattern).
- Tab already toggles hierarchy expand/collapse for items with children — that behaviour must not regress.
- The renderer must never exceed `rows - 1` lines (pane line-count invariant, WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO).

## Existing state

- Group separators are rendered by `createListRenderer` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` when the `group` field changes between items in the flattened list; they are derived at render time and are NOT rows in any navigation model.
- Navigation (`WorkItemListState.moveUp/moveDown/pageUp/pageDown`, `_clampSelection`, `_adjustScroll`, `flatCount`) indexes into the flattened items list, so headings are never selected.
- Tab maps to the `'toggle-expand'` action (`keyToAction`), which expands/collapses top-level items with children; the main TUI loop fetches children on demand for that action.
- Group assignments come from `regroupWorkItems` (packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts), which stamps every selected item with a numeric `group` and a `groupLabel` (`Critical Group N`, `Group N`, `Idea`, `Other`, `In Review`).

## Desired change

Introduce a first-class **display-rows model** in `WorkItemListState` that interleaves heading rows with item rows:

- New heading entry type (e.g. `{ kind: 'heading', group, groupLabel, count, collapsed }`) produced by a `getDisplayRows()`-style method over the flattened items (children of expanded parents included; items of collapsed groups excluded).
- Navigation, clamping, and scrolling operate over display rows so the cursor lands on headings; `getSelectedItem()` returns `null` for a heading selection (metadata panel then renders group info).
- New collapsed-groups state (`Set<number>` in memory) with toggle on Tab when a heading row is selected; refresh carries the set over (by group number, mirroring `expandedItems` handling).
- `createListRenderer` renders heading rows directly from the display model (label + `(count)` + collapse arrow) and stops deriving separators from group transitions; the visible-window budget logic (`countSeparators`) is reworked for heading rows.
- Tab routing: heading row → toggle group; item row → existing expand/collapse-children path (including the on-demand children fetch in the TUI loop).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — display-rows model, heading type, collapse state, navigation over rows, Tab routing, renderer heading rows + counts.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — heading rendering (counts, collapse arrow), navigation onto/over headings, Tab toggle, metadata panel on heading selection.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts` — collapsed groups survive refresh; Tab-on-item children fetch unaffected.

## Assumptions

- "Headings" = the group separator rows (`── <Group Label> ──`) produced by `regroupWorkItems` group assignments. No other heading type exists in the list.
- Count = top-level items in the group in the current view; children of expanded parents do not add to the count (they never carry group metadata).
- Count is shown whether the group is collapsed or expanded.
- Enter on a heading is a no-op; Tab is the only toggle key (per request).
- Collapsed state is in-memory only, consistent with `expandedItems` (no settings persistence).
- Collapse keyed by group number; if a refresh regroups and renumbers groups, the collapsed set may apply to a shifted group — acceptable in-session, same class of behaviour as `expandedItems`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** extending this to the Pi TUI Worklog extension or persisting collapse state to settings would expand scope — record such follow-ups as separate work items rather than folding them in.
- **Regression risk:** reworking the navigation model from `flatCount` (items only) to display rows touches clamping, scroll adjustment, wrap-around, refresh selection-restore, and the renderer's line budget — the existing expand/refresh and line-count tests must stay green.

## Related work

- WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW — Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order): introduced the render-time group separators this feature builds on.
- WL-0MSAKPVR9005B6XJ — Rewrite assignItemGroups + next.ts ordering: canonical group ordering/labelling used by the headings.
- WL-0MS8XOOMN0022LLH — Pi TUI browse flow: re-fetch + heading count: heading counts exist in the Pi TUI browse widget; Herdr parity for counts.
- WL-0MS4L81QF0013081 — Tab key to expand/collapse children in selection browser: established the Tab expand/collapse pattern this feature extends.
- WL-0MSBVBNGH002RDP5 — Herdr worklist: expanded items momentarily collapse on list refresh (flicker): refresh/children handling this feature must preserve.
- WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO — pane line-count invariant (renderer budget) this feature's heading-row accounting must preserve.
- WL-0MS39YPR5005MJ81 — Feature gap analysis: Pi TUI Worklog extension vs Herdr plugin: prior comparison of the two selection lists (find_related automated match).

Automated find_related report: full (untruncated) version persisted at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should up/down navigation land on heading rows? — Answer (operator): the request notes "moving up and down does not select the heading lines" as the current gap; selectable headings are required for Tab-on-heading to work, so the feature includes heading selection. Source: interactive request.
- Q: What does the count show? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): top-level items in the group, current view, both collapsed and expanded. Source: reasonable default consistent with the data model.
- Q: Should collapsed state persist across restarts? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): no — in-memory like `expandedItems`. Source: consistent with existing hierarchy expand state.

# Feature Request / Bug: FTS index freshness + silent query-error swallowing

## Problem statement

`wl search` help advertises "Full-text search over work items (title, description, comments, tags)" — and comment indexing is implemented and *works after a manual rebuild* (verified: column-scoped `comments:"Closed with reason"` MATCH returns rows; 1,567/2,462 indexed rows contain comment text; `wl search '"v0.1.11"'` returns comment matches). Two defects make comment search unreliable in practice:

1. **The FTS index is never updated incrementally.** `upsertFtsEntry(item)` (dist/persistent-store.js:963) is defined but has **zero call sites** — it is dead code. `saveWorkItem` / `saveComment` do not touch `worklog_fts`. The index only refreshes via the manual `wl search --rebuild-index` command. Any work item or comment created/edited since the last rebuild is invisible to search — silently stale results (recent items/comments missing, duplicates not detected by triage heuristics).

2. **Malformed FTS5 queries fail silently.** An unquoted punctuated query such as `wl search v0.1.11` produces an FTS5 syntax error (`fts5: syntax error near "."`) that the catch block (persistent-store.js ~1157) swallows, returning `[]` with no warning. Users cannot distinguish "no matches" from "invalid query". Version strings, file paths, and ids (all common search targets in this tool) are exactly the strings that trip this.

## User stories

- As an agent deduplicating test-failure work items, I want recently added comments and items to appear in `wl search` without requiring a manual `--rebuild-index`, so I don't create duplicates.
- As a user searching for `v0.1.11` or a file path, I want either correct matches or an explicit "invalid query" error, not a silent empty result.

## Expected behaviour

- Creating/updating a work item or adding/deleting a comment keeps the FTS index current (call `upsertFtsEntry` from the save paths; call `deleteFtsEntry` from item/comment delete paths).
- FTS5 query syntax errors are surfaced to the user (non-zero exit + clear message), not swallowed; only genuinely zero-match queries return empty results.
- Consider quoting/escaping hygiene: document (and optionally auto-quote) punctuated terms; an option like `--rebuild-index` remains as the backstop for bulk migrations.
- Optional: automatic index rebuild (or per-item reindex) when the index is detected empty/stale (e.g. hash-based staleness already used for embeddings).

## Suggested implementation approach

1. Wire `upsertFtsEntry` into `saveWorkItem` (dist/persistent-store.js:299) and into `saveComment`/comment-delete paths (comments currently don't trigger any FTS update at all).
2. Change `searchFts`'s catch block to rethrow/flag syntax errors (or validate the query with a dry MATCH first) so the command layer can report `error: invalid query syntax` with the offending term.
3. Add unit tests: new item searchable immediately after save; new comment searchable immediately after add; punctuated query error surfaces; delete removes from index.

## Acceptance criteria

1. After `wl create` + `wl comment add`, both the title and the comment text are found by `wl search` WITHOUT running `--rebuild-index`.
2. `wl search v0.1.11` (unquoted punctuated term) exits non-zero with a clear "invalid query — quote phrases" message instead of silently returning 0.
3. Deleting an item/comment removes it from subsequent search results.
4. `wl search --rebuild-index` still works as the manual backstop; full test suite passes.

## Related work

- related-to: SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ (SorraAgents) — its analysis assumed comments were not searchable; this request resolves that gap and would enable comment-based remediation queries (e.g. `shipped in v1.0.0` close-reason sweep).
- related-to: WL-0MSLW8GHQ0092PJK — `--fields` projection for list/search; both improve wl CLI efficiency.
data.title: FTS search: keep index fresh (wire upsertFtsEntry into save paths) and surface query syntax errors

## Problem

When using the `a-r` shortcut to manually reject an `in_review` item, the current command only sets `reviewed` to `false` and marks `ready-to-close` as `no`. The item stays in its current status and stage, which doesn't allow for easy rework.

## Current Behavior

The `a-r` shortcut in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` runs:

```
!!wl reviewed <id> false && wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no --summary 'Rejected by manual review. <reason>'
```

This leaves the item in its current status and stage.

## User Story

As a producer reviewing work items, when I reject an item using `a-r`, I expect it to be reset to an active state so it can be reworked.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When `a-r` is triggered on an item in `in_review` stage, the item's status changes to `open`
2. The item's stage changes to `plan_complete`
3. The item's priority changes to `medium`
4. The existing `reviewed false` and `audit-set` logic is preserved
5. All existing tests for the `a-r` shortcut continue to pass

# Show complete, right-aligned model name on footer Line 3 (remove 30-col truncation)

## Problem statement

The Worklog extension's custom TUI footer Line 3 (session-health) displays the session's model identifier (e.g. `code → openai/gpt-4`) on the right side of the line, but the identifier is capped at 30 visible columns and truncated with an ellipsis (`code → openai/gpt-4-abcdefghij…`), and it is not flush-right — it sits directly after the `│` separator that follows the command preview. The operator wants the full model name visible (never truncated) and right-aligned to the terminal edge.

## Users

End users of the Pi TUI with the Worklog extension enabled, including herdr-spawned pi panes. The footer Line 3 is the at-a-glance readout of which model is serving the session. A truncated model name is hard to read/verify; right-alignment gives the readout a stable, scannable position at the terminal edge.

User story: "As a pi user, I want to see the full resolved model name (e.g. `openai/gpt-4-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz`) without truncation, flush right on the footer line, so I can always verify exactly which model is serving my session."

## Acceptance Criteria

- The model identifier (selected alias → resolved provider/model, `(resolving)`, resolved-only, or `—`) is always rendered in full on footer Line 3 — the 30-column `modelPartMaxWidth` cap (and its ellipsis truncation) is removed.
- The model identifier is right-aligned: its right edge is flush with the terminal's right edge (line width). When an initial prompt preview exists, it stays left-aligned with padding between the preview and the model; when no prompt exists, the model alone is padded to the right edge.
- The command/prompt preview yields space to the model: the preview is truncated (with `...`) as needed so the full model name fits; the model name is never truncated by the budget logic.
- Safety clamp at ultra-narrow widths: if the full model name plus separator cannot fit alongside the prompt, the prompt (and then the separator) is dropped before any part of the model; only when the model name alone exceeds the terminal width is the final `truncateToTerminalWidth(…, width)` clamp allowed to clip it (physically unavoidable).
- Footer Lines 1–2 (extension statuses, session health) and the no-model `—` fallback are unchanged.
- Unit tests in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.test.ts` ("model line in footer") are updated: assert full (untruncated) model rendering, right-edge alignment (model's visible right edge at `width`), prompt truncation/yield behavior, and the narrow-width safety clamp; the full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Change only footer Line 3 rendering in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` (the `render()` function inside `setFooter`); do not alter Lines 1–2, the herdr pane, or `model-display.ts`.
- Preserve the grey/dim styling, the `│` separator, the `truncateWorkItemId` compaction of the prompt preview, and terminal-width-aware measuring (`visibleWidth` / `truncateToTerminalWidth`).
- Keep the change surgical: no refactoring of unrelated code.

## Existing state

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — custom footer via `ctx.ui.setFooter()`. Line 3 currently: builds `modelPart` (`alias → provider/model`, `(resolving)`, `—` fallbacks), caps it with `const modelPartMaxWidth = 30; cappedModelPart = truncateToTerminalWidth(modelPart, 30)`, then composes `${promptPart}${separator}${cappedModelPart}` and pushes `truncateToTerminalWidth(theme.fg('dim', label), width)`. The prompt budget is `width − modelWidth − separatorWidth`, so the model cap of 30 guarantees the prompt gets most of the line.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.test.ts` — "model line in footer" describe block asserts: exact string `'Fix the bug by adding validation  │  code → openai/gpt-4'`; commandPart > modelPart measurement; the 30-col cap case (asserts NOT containing `qrstuvwxyz`); narrow-width no-overflow; prompt truncation with `...  │  code →`; model-only cases.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/terminal-utils.ts` — provides `visibleWidth()` and `truncateToTerminalWidth()` (already imported).

## Desired change

In `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` (footer `render()`), Line 3 composition:

1. Build `modelPart` exactly as today (alias → resolved model, `(resolving)`, `—` fallbacks); drop `modelPartMaxWidth`/`cappedModelPart` and use `modelPart` untruncated.
2. Compute `modelWidth = visibleWidth(modelPart)` and `separatorWidth = visibleWidth(separator)`.
3. Prompt budget = `max(0, width − modelWidth − separatorWidth)`; truncate the compacted prompt preview to that budget with `...` as today.
4. Compose `label = promptPart ? `${promptPart}${separator}${modelPart}` : modelPart`.
5. Right-align: insert padding between the prompt and the separator (or leading padding when there is no prompt) so the model's visible right edge equals `width` — pad = `width − visibleWidth(promptPart) − separatorWidth − modelWidth` (or `width − modelWidth` for the no-prompt case); drop the prompt/separator first if there is no room, then apply the final `truncateToTerminalWidth(…, width)` safety clamp.

## Key Files

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — Line-3 label composition, right-alignment padding, and budget logic (primary change).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.test.ts` — update "model line in footer" tests for full model rendering + right alignment; add right-edge assertion and prompt-yield cases.

## Related work

- WL-0MSHENVKR002HZT5 — "Swap model identifier and command positions on herd status line" (completed): introduced the current Line-3 layout (command left, model right) and the 30-column model cap this item removes.
- WL-0MRF6JXMD003KHLQ — "Show initial prompt preview in footer info line" (completed): introduced the prompt preview on Line 3.
- WL-0MRF19R71004YJND — "Add model/provider line to TUI status bar footer" (completed): introduced the model footer line.
- WL-0MRDRZ32L00404D0 — "Session Health Extension for Pi Footer" (completed): the custom footer this change lives in.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "thrdr plugin" = the Worklog extension's session-health footer Line 3 (the only surface that displays the model name; it renders in pi panes spawned by herdr). Recorded in the Appendix; if the operator meant a different surface, revisit.
- Assumption: "right aligned" = model's right edge flush with the terminal's right edge (width), with the prompt preview left-aligned and padding between. Recorded in the Appendix.
- Edge case: a model name longer than the entire terminal width cannot be fully displayed; the final clamp clips it (documented in AC4 as physically unavoidable). All other cases show the model complete.
- Scope-creep risk: no adjacent polish (e.g. separator style, prompt truncation style) — out of scope unless it blocks right-alignment.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which surface is 'thrdr plugin'?" — Answer (repo inspection, no interactive reply needed): the Worklog Pi extension's custom footer Line 3 (`session-health.ts`), the only place a model name is displayed; it renders in herdr-spawned pi panes. Source: grep of `packages/herdr/src/` (no model display) and `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` (Line 3 model display). Prior item WL-0MSHENVKR002HZT5 resolved the same ambiguity ("herd status line" = pi TUI footer model line).
- Q: "What does 'right aligned' mean given the model is already on the right side?" — Answer (interpretation, recorded as assumption): the model should be flush with the right edge of the terminal, with the prompt preview left-aligned and flexible padding between them. Today the model sits directly after the separator at a variable position. No user clarification requested — the pairing with "complete (not truncated)" makes the intent clear; flagged as assumption in Risks & assumptions.
- Q: "When the full model name competes with the prompt preview for width, which wins?" — Answer (interpretation): the model name wins; the prompt preview (already a truncated preview) yields space first. Recorded as AC2/AC4. The request's emphasis on "complete (not truncated)" model name supports this; flagged as assumption.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRERDU1J000W1IS** – Show time since last streaming chunk in session health footer (completed)
- **WL-0MRO7LWIX001516P** – Show model status in pi quickly (completed)
- **WL-0MS4FHW290053SH4** – Missing text-insertion shortcuts (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-Show-complete-right-aligned-model-name-on-footer-Line-3-WL-0MSMDYJ3X00895MP.md` — matched: 0mrdrz32l00404d0, 0mrf19r71004yjnd, 0mrf6jxmd003khlq, 0mshenvkr002hzt5, abcdefghij (+296 more)

# Herdr plugin: activity-gated proxy mode switching (cheap on operator idle, fast on operator command)

## Problem statement

The llama-proxy runs in two operating modes — **fast** (cloud-backed, 3-slot pool) and **cheap** (2-slot local-first pool). Today mode is switched manually (admin API/UI) or on a fixed time schedule; there is no link between *operator presence* and mode. When an operator is actively working through the herdr plugin, every Pi command should be served by **fast** mode; when the operator leaves (no agent-route Pi commands through the plugin for a configurable window), the proxy should drop to **cheap** mode so the downtime worker's autonomous dispatches consume only the cheap local pool.

## Users

- **Operator running the herdr worklog plugin + llama-proxy** — wants fast responses while actively working and zero-cost cheap mode when away, without touching the mode API by hand.

Example user stories:

- *"As an operator, when I issue an agent command (/skill:*, /intake, /plan, /prompt:) through the herdr plugin, I want the proxy switched to fast mode immediately so my session is served by the cloud-backed pool."*
- *"As an operator, when I have issued no agent-route Pi commands through the plugin for 15 minutes, I want the proxy switched to cheap mode (only when it is idle) so the downtime dispatcher's work runs on the cheap local pool."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Operator-activity tracking:** the plugin records a timestamp on every **agent-route** command (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:` — the routes that spawn a pi agent pane); shell shortcuts (`!!`/`!`) and plain commands do NOT count as operator activity.
- [ ] **Cheap switch on idle:** when no operator agent-route command has been routed for ≥ `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` (default `900000` = 15 min, configurable) **AND** the proxy reports idle (reusing the existing `/llama/local/status` idle evaluation: llama-server running, no active local query, no model switch, no local lease, all required slots free), the worker POSTs `/admin/set-mode {"mode":"cheap"}`. A busy proxy (active local query) **delays** the switch (never kills in-flight work).
- [ ] **Fast switch on command:** when a new operator agent-route command is routed through the plugin, it immediately POSTs `/admin/set-mode {"mode":"fast"}` (fire-and-forget; a failed switch never blocks or delays the command dispatch — the pane opens regardless, fail-open).
- [ ] **No redundant switching / no hammering:** the worker skips a switch when the persisted mode already matches the target (track last-known mode; refresh via `GET /admin/mode` on poll). At most one switch per state change; a `409` (mode-switch restart in progress) is treated as a no-op and retried on a later tick.
- [ ] **Fail-closed everywhere:** endpoint failures, timeouts, network errors, and ambiguous responses yield no switch and never crash or block the plugin. On plugin restart the idle clock resets to "active now" (fail-safe: the proxy stays fast until a fresh full idle window passes).
- [ ] **Configurable via plugin settings** (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`): enabled toggle, idle threshold ms, poll interval ms; settings re-read every tick so changes apply without a plugin restart. The proxy URL is shared with the downtime worker (`downtimeProxyUrl`).
- [ ] **Coexistence with the proxy's built-in schedule:** the plugin's switches are manual overrides (the API's native semantics, LP-0MSMF25V9002AY1J); the proxy's time-based schedule (cheap 01:00–10:00, fast 10:00–01:00) reclaims control at its next boundary. Documented behavior, not a conflict.
- [ ] **Testing & validation:** unit tests cover idle-window evaluation, last-command tracking, cheap/fast switch triggers, restart reset, fail-closed paths, and settings clamps. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the herdr README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only **agent-route** commands count as operator activity (operator decision Q1).
- The cheap switch is gated on proxy idle — it must never kill in-flight work (operator decision Q4b).
- Mode switches never block the TUI or command dispatch: all HTTP calls are fire-and-forget (fast switch) or scheduled task work (cheap switch).
- Fail-closed at every boundary: no crash, no hammering, no repeated identical POSTs.
- The seed mentions "the `/admin/mode` API": `GET /admin/mode` only *reads* the mode; the switch endpoint is `POST /admin/set-mode`. The brief targets `/admin/set-mode`.

## Existing state

- Mode API + UI exist on the proxy: `GET /admin/mode`, `POST /admin/set-mode` (LP-0MSLMYEEU002IBH6); mode persisted in `proxy/.mode`, defaults to `fast`.
- Time-based automatic mode switching exists on the proxy (cheap 01:00–10:00, fast 10:00–01:00, LP-0MSM5K4TX004MICX) with manual-override persistence until the next scheduled change (LP-0MSMF25V9002AY1J). A mode switch restarts the proxy (terminates in-flight requests; clients retry — documented accepted behavior).
- The herdr plugin already has: settings system (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`, re-read per tick), a consolidated scheduler (worklist.ts), and a downtime worker that polls `/llama/local/status` with fail-closed idle evaluation (WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K + children). The mode-switch worker reuses this infrastructure.

## Desired change

Add a mode-switch worker to the herdr plugin:

1. `index.ts` `onCommand` (agent route) records `lastOperatorCommandAt = Date.now()` and fires the fast switch (`POST /admin/set-mode {"mode":"fast"}`, fire-and-forget, fail-open).
2. A new scheduler task (pattern-matched on the existing `downtime` task) ticks on `modeSwitchPollIntervalMs`: if `lastOperatorCommandAt` is null/older than the threshold AND the proxy is idle (reuse the local-status poller/idle evaluation), POST `/admin/set-mode {"mode":"cheap"}` — skipping when the persisted mode already is cheap.
3. New settings: `modeSwitchEnabled`, `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs`, `modeSwitchPollIntervalMs` (reusing `downtimeProxyUrl`); re-read each tick.
4. Restart behavior: worker construction sets `lastOperatorCommandAt = Date.now()` (reset to active).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` — new worker: idle-window evaluation, mode-state tracking, `/admin/set-mode` HTTP client (POST) + `GET /admin/mode` read, fail-closed
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` — unit tests (test-first)
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — new settings keys + clamps + defaults
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — scheduler task wiring + TUI options plumbing
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — agent-route hook: record last-command timestamp + fire fast switch
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — settings and behavior documentation

## Related work

- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** — "Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime" (parent of the downtime worker; the poller/settings/scheduler infrastructure this feature reuses)
- **LP-0MSLMYEEU002IBH6** (llm-manager) — Web API/UI to toggle fast/cheap modes (the `/admin/mode` + `/admin/set-mode` endpoints)
- **LP-0MSM5K4TX004MICX** (llm-manager) — Time-based automatic mode switching (built-in schedule)
- **LP-0MSMF25V9002AY1J** (llm-manager) — API mode override persists until the next scheduled change
- **WL-0MSMIPPJI007GU9N / LP-0MSMZOAJW002UR2A** (llm-manager) — cheap-mode profile definition (2-slot pool)
- find-related automated report: WL-0MRCTZZ82000X7TM, WL-0MP15AMKV002F3U4, WL-0MS6AAW3M004JK9U (weak keyword matches; not design-relevant)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Mode switch restarts the proxy** (kills in-flight requests). Mitigated for the cheap direction by the idle gate (Q4b); the fast direction can still kill a cheap-mode downtime request when the operator returns — accepted (documented proxy behavior; the downtime dispatch's work retries on the next idle period).
- **Multiple plugin panes** could each run a mode-switch worker → duplicate POSTs. Same-mode POSTs are API noops and the worker skips already-matching modes, so the system converges; per-process single-flight is applied.
- **Schedule reassertion at boundaries** may flip the mode shortly after a plugin switch near a boundary — accepted; every new operator command re-switches to fast immediately (design intent).
- **`GET /admin/mode`/`POST /admin/set-mode` may not be reachable** from the plugin host — fail-closed (no switch), never crash; the plugin logs a warning.
- **Scope-creep risk:** related but out-of-scope opportunities (e.g., reflecting the active mode in the herdr UI, per-slot idle gating for the cheap switch, or activity-based mode tracking for non-plugin pi panes) are recorded as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption:** "operator-issued Pi command" ≡ agent-route commands routed through the herdr plugin (Q1). Commands issued directly in a pi pane (not via the plugin) are out of scope.
- **Assumption:** the existing idle evaluation (`evaluateIdle` with `requiredFreeSlots = 0`, all slots free) is the busy/idle gate for the cheap switch; if per-slot data later arrives (WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG), the gate follows the same semantics.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should only the agent-route commands (/skill:*, /intake, /plan, /prompt: → new pi pane) count as 'operator Pi commands' for the idle timer, or any command routed through the plugin?" — Answer (operator): "only agent-route". Source: interactive reply. Research: `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` `routeCommand`/`isAgentCommand` distinguishes agent vs pane vs stdout routes.
- Q2: "Should the herdr plugin's activity-based switching (a) coexist as manual overrides — the schedule eventually reclaims control — or (b) fully own the mode while enabled?" — Answer (operator): clarified intent: "if the operator issues an agent-command it is *always* processed as 'fast', but if the operator leaves and the downtime dispatcher starts sending commands they are 'cheap'." Interpretation recorded: plugin switches are immediate manual overrides (fast on command, cheap on idle); the proxy's time schedule remains as a background fallback (coexistence, option a). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "After a plugin restart, should the idle clock (a) reset to 'active now' — stay fast until a fresh full idle window — or (b) treat restart as idle and switch to cheap immediately?" — Answer (operator): "a". Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Cheap-switch gating vs proxy busy state: (a) switch at the threshold unconditionally (can kill in-flight downtime dispatch), or (b) switch only when the proxy also reports idle?" — Answer (operator): "b". Source: interactive reply. Research: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `evaluateIdle`/`isIdleStatus`; `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/handlers.py` `/admin/set-mode` restart semantics.

# Intake brief: Herdr — flipping `needsProducerReview` must not make a valid audit stale

**Work item:** WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R (bug, medium)

## Problem statement

Flipping the `needsProducerReview` flag (e.g. `wl update <id> --needs-producer-review true`, as the heartbeat does when flagging an item for producer review) bumps the work item's `updatedAt`. herdr's audit-freshness predicate `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` then reports the previously valid audit as **stale**, which (a) degrades the TUI audit icon from the passed glyph to the stale-passed/stage glyph, and (b) makes the downtime audit tier re-select the item for a wasteful `/skill:audit` re-run of unchanged content. A review-state flag is metadata, not content — it must not invalidate an audit.

## Users

- **Producer** — flips `needsProducerReview` (via TUI flag toggle or `wl update --needs-producer-review`) to signal review intent. Should see the item's existing green "audit passed" state unchanged.
  - User story: "As a producer, when I flag an item for review, I want its audit result to remain visibly passed, so I can trust that only genuinely changed items need re-auditing."
- **Herdr downtime worker** — dispatches `/skill:audit` for items without a valid audit during idle time. Should not burn an audit run on items whose only change since the audit was a review flag.
  - User story: "As the audit-tier dispatcher, I want to skip items whose audit is stale only because of a metadata flag flip, so idle time is spent auditing items whose content actually changed."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `WorklogDatabase.update()` persists a `needsProducerReview`-only change but **preserves** `updatedAt` (no bump). A change to any content field (title, description, status, stage, priority, sortIndex, parentId, tags, assignee, issueType, risk, effort) still bumps `updatedAt` exactly as today.
- [ ] Unit test (packages/shared): `update()` with only `needsProducerReview` flipped → flag persisted, `updatedAt` unchanged.
- [ ] Unit test (packages/shared): `update()` with a content field + flag in the same call → `updatedAt` bumped (combined update still bumps).
- [ ] Regression (packages/shared): no-op update and content-only update behave exactly as today (no-op preserves, content bumps).
- [ ] Herdr integration verification: after a flag-only update, `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` remains **true** for a previously fresh audit → TUI shows the passed icon (not the stale glyph) and `selectAuditCandidate` does **not** select the item (no redundant `/skill:audit` dispatch). Herdr code itself is unchanged (single source of truth stays in worklog).
- [ ] Documentation: comment on `update()`/the `fieldsToCompare` split documents why `needsProducerReview` is excluded from the timestamp-bump trigger; the `isAuditFresh` doc comment in `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` notes the guarantee ("flag-only flips do not move `updatedAt`").
- [ ] All related documentation updated (code comments, README/docs as applicable).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix must live in the **worklog core** (`packages/shared/src/database.ts` `update()`), per operator decision — not in herdr. herdr's `isAuditFresh` and `selectAuditCandidate` stay untouched; they automatically benefit once `updatedAt` stops moving on flag flips.
- Do not change the meaning of `updatedAt` for content changes: sync field-conflict resolution ("newer `updatedAt` wins", `src/sync.ts`) and `wl recent` ordering rely on it. Accepted caveat (operator-approved): a flag-only flip no longer bumps `updatedAt`, so a concurrent remote content edit could out-rank the flag in a field-conflict merge (low severity — the flag is a review signal, not content).
- The no-op fast path (`hasChanged` false → preserve `updatedAt`, no store write) must remain; the flag-only path must still **write** the flag while preserving the timestamp (it must not take the early return).
- `needsProducerReview` is the only field moved to the no-bump set; no other fields change semantics (minimal, surgical).
- Out of scope: the audit skill's own pipeline freshness (already handled by the content-fingerprint gate, SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT — a flag flip doesn't change the fingerprint); WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE (at-or-near freshness for the audit's own persistence write) is a separate item.

## Existing state

1. `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `update()`: `fieldsToCompare` includes `needsProducerReview`; if any tracked field changed → `updated.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()`.
2. `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)`: `auditTime > updateTime - 60000` (60 s buffer). A post-audit `updatedAt` bump → not fresh → stale.
3. `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` `getIconPrefix()` (line ~367): for `in_review`, `fresh ? auditIcon(...) : (auditResult === true ? auditStaleIcon(...) : stageIcon(...))` — the stale glyph path.
4. `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `selectAuditCandidate()` (line ~1043): filters `!isAuditFresh(c.auditedAt, c.updatedAt)` → stale item becomes an audit-dispatch candidate (subject to 7-day recency window and dispatched-marker exclusion).
5. `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` `getNextAuditCandidate()` (line ~371): audit tier pulls candidates from `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` and routes through `selectAuditCandidate`.
6. Heartbeat (`skill/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py`) flags the next ready item via `wl update <id> --needs-producer-review true` — the trigger of the reported symptom.

## Desired change

In `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `update()`, split the change detection:

- `contentFieldsToCompare` = current `fieldsToCompare` **minus** `needsProducerReview` — any change here bumps `updatedAt` (unchanged behavior).
- `needsProducerReview` is a **metadata** field: a flag-only change persists the flag but preserves `updatedAt` (does not take the no-op early return, and does not bump the timestamp).
- Combined content+flag change → bump (as today).
- herdr: **no code change**; add/refresh a doc comment on `isAuditFresh` stating the guarantee and re-verify the icon + dispatch behavior via tests in `packages/herdr`.

## Key Files:

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `WorklogDatabase.update()`; split `fieldsToCompare` into content (bump) vs metadata (`needsProducerReview`, preserve `updatedAt`); keep the no-op fast path distinct from the flag-only path
- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` (or existing shared test location) — new unit tests: flag-only (persist, preserve), content+flag (bump), no-op, content-only (unchanged behavior)
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — doc comment on `isAuditFresh` (guarantee: flag-only flips do not move `updatedAt`); no logic change
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — no change; referenced for verification that `selectAuditCandidate` stops selecting flag-staled items
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.test.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — integration-style regression checks (fresh audit after flag-only update → passed icon, not a dispatch candidate)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Sync conflict (accepted, low):** `src/sync.ts` field-conflict resolution picks the newer `updatedAt`; a flag-only flip no longer bumps it, so a concurrent remote content edit could out-rank the flag in a conflict merge. Mitigation: the flag is a review signal, not content — re-flagging is cheap and the next sync merge reconciles. Operator-approved in Q1.
- **`wl recent` ordering:** `src/commands/recent.ts` sorts by `updatedAt`; flag flips will no longer surface items as "recently updated". Arguably more correct (a review flag is not activity); document in the change notes.
- **Herdr dispatch recency window:** a flag-only flip no longer extends the 7-day audit-recency window (`DOWNTIME_AUDIT_RECENCY_WINDOW_MS`) — an old item flagged for review stays outside the window, unchanged from today (recency is about content activity, not review intent).
- **Scope-creep guard:** WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE (at-or-near freshness for the audit's own persistence write) is a separate item — do not fold it in here. The alternative "content-version signal" approach (Q1 option B) is explicitly out of scope.
- **Assumption:** herdr is the only timestamp-freshness consumer that matters for this bug; `heartbeat.py` checks `wl audit-show` rawOutput ("Ready to close: Yes"), not freshness, so it is unaffected either way.

## Related work

- WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE (open, bug, medium) — "Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher": *opposite direction* (audit's own persistence write must not look stale). Shares the same `isAuditFresh` predicate; complement, not duplicate. Coordinate so the two fixes don't conflict on the predicate.
- WL-0MS1OJZL7005CR7A (completed) — "Show distinct icon when audit is stale but readyToClose is true": introduced the stale-passed icon behavior.
- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG (completed) — "Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit": the audit-tier dispatch feature.
- WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31 (completed) — "Audit candidate selection".
- SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT (SorraAgents) — content-fingerprint freshness gate in the audit runner; the pipeline-side precedent for "non-content updates must not invalidate an audit".
- WL-0MLGTWT4S1X4HDD9 / WL-0MLQ0ZHQE0JBX8Y6 (completed) — `--needs-producer-review` filter and TUI shortcut; the flag feature this fix interacts with.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should the fix live? (A) Worklog core — `wl update` persists a `needsProducerReview`-only change but preserves `updatedAt` (flag is metadata, not content), fixing herdr display + dispatch with one change; caveat: sync field-conflict resolution could drop a flag flip racing a concurrent remote content edit. (B) Herdr-side only — requires worklog to emit a new content-version signal (bigger). (C) Both / other." — Answer (user): **A — Worklog core**. Source: interactive reply. Research: `WorklogDatabase.update()` (packages/shared/src/database.ts) is the single write path for `wl update`; herdr's `isAuditFresh`/`selectAuditCandidate` consume only timestamps, so preserving `updatedAt` on flag-only writes fixes both consumers without herdr changes.
- Q2: "Scope — the stale audit shows up in herdr as (1) TUI icon degradation and (2) re-dispatch of `/skill:audit`. Cover both (shared predicate), or only dispatch?" — Answer (user): **Both**. Source: interactive reply. Research: both effects derive from the same `isAuditFresh` predicate (icons.ts:250, used at icons.ts:367 and downtime-worker.ts:1043); fixing the root cause (no `updatedAt` bump) resolves both; herdr-side regression tests verify both paths.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQ3LYSPS006V60H** – TUI does not auto-refresh after CLI audit update (completed)
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** – Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon (completed)
- **WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ** – Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the selection list (open)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — audit/auditedAt/isAuditFresh/freshness/updatedAt/stale semantics documented in the herdr package README
