# Feature Request: tolerant work-item ID resolution in `wl show` for agent tool use

## Problem statement

The SorraAgents audit skill ships `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py find-workitem <id>`,
which resolves a work item by shelling out to `wl search <id> --json` and then
post-filtering the results for an exact id match. Agents are directed to this
wrapper because the native wl CLI has no single command that tolerantly
resolves a work-item ID:

- `wl show <id>` is exact-match only (`db.get(normalizedId)`); a partial,
  case-differing, or truncated ID fails with "Work item not found".
- `wl list <term>` performs case-insensitive **substring** matching over
  id/title/description — this is the optimal substring-search primitive — but
  returns a list of matches, not a single resolved item.
- `wl search <query>` is full-text search (FTS, token/prefix-based) — it is
  NOT a substring matcher.

So there is a gap: no single native command does "given an ID reference,
resolve the item" with tolerant (exact-first, unique-substring-fallback)
matching. This feature closes that gap so agent tooling (and humans) can use
one native command instead of a wrapper.

## User story

As an agent (or user) holding an ID reference that may be exact, truncated, or
partial, I want `wl show` to resolve it tolerantly — exact match first, then a
unique case-insensitive substring match on the id — with a clear structured
error when the reference is ambiguous — so I can resolve a work item with a
single native `wl show` call.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl show <id> --json` returns the work item when `<id>` matches an item id
   exactly (current behavior preserved, including `normalizeCliId` case/prefix
   normalization).
2. When no exact id matches but exactly one work item's **id** contains `<id>`
   case-insensitively as a substring, `wl show` resolves to that item and
   returns `success: true` with the item (JSON mode), with no error.
3. When multiple items match (ambiguous), `wl show` exits non-zero with a
   structured error `ambiguous-match` listing the candidate ids in JSON mode,
   and a human-readable disambiguation hint otherwise.
4. When nothing matches, `wl show` keeps the existing "Work item not found"
   behavior (non-zero exit, structured error in JSON mode).
5. `--json` output remains machine-parseable in all three outcome paths
   (found / ambiguous / not found).
6. New vitest coverage for: exact match, unique substring match, ambiguous
   match, and not-found — in both JSON and human output modes.
7. Documentation updated (CLI.md / EXAMPLES.md / docs command reference) to
   describe the tolerant resolution and the `ambiguous-match` error.

## Design notes (suggested, not prescriptive)

- Resolution order: exact id (via `normalizeCliId`) → unique case-insensitive
  substring match over item ids → ambiguity/not-found handling. Keep the
  fallback scoped to the **id** field (not title/description) to minimise
  surprise ambiguity; `wl list <term>` remains the canonical way to search
  title/description substrings.
- Reuse the existing `db.list()` substring filter logic from `list.ts` for the
  fallback so behaviour stays consistent.
- Consider a `--exact` flag to force strict exact-match behaviour for callers
  that need it.

## Out of scope

- No change to `wl list <term>` substring semantics (already canonical).
- No change to `wl search` (FTS) behaviour or index.
- No semantic/embedding matching.

## Related

- Unblocks: SorraAgents work item "Replace scan.py find-workitem with native
  wl CLI lookup in audit prompts" (tracked in the SorraAgents worklog; this
  item is its blocker).
- Context: SorraAgents SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI refined audit prompt guidance to
  `wl list <term> --json` (substring) + `scan.py find-workitem <id>` (exact,
  interim) for worklog lookups; scan.py find-workitem is the wrapper this
  feature replaces.
data.title: Add tolerant work-item ID resolution to wl show (exact-first, unique substring fallback, ambiguity error) for agent tool use

# Lower downtime worker idle threshold + poll interval

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime worker (`createDowntimeWorker` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) only dispatches local-LLM work after the local model has been **continuously idle for the full idle threshold**, default `DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 240_000` (4 min), polled every `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000` (30s). Analysis of llama-proxy logs (2026-08-11 overnight, 01:00-11:57) shows the local model busy only 43.6% of the time, with long stretches of partial idle (03:00-10:00 avg 0.87-1.33 slots busy of 2). Every idle gap shorter than 4 minutes is currently skipped — those gaps are missed local-dispatch opportunities that instead go to remote providers.

Goal: maximize local LLM utilization by dispatching into shorter idle gaps.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` lowered from 240_000 to 60_000 (60s), with the `clampDowntimeIdleThresholdMs` floor (1s) unchanged.
2. `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` lowered from 30_000 to 10_000 (the existing `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_FLOOR_MS` floor), so idle onset is detected faster.
3. Existing test suite updated: clamps still enforce floors (10s poll floor, 1s threshold floor); idle-threshold timing tests use the new default; no test asserts the old 240s/30s values.
4. Settings persistence unchanged (defaults flow through `defaultSettings`); deployed `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` is untouched (only `browseItemCount` set today — defaults apply).
5. Full project test suite passes (quiet mode).

## Notes

- A race (dispatch fires as an interactive request arrives) is acceptable: the agent request simply falls back to remote, same as today — worst case is no worse than the status quo.
- The audit tier's subprocess fan-out and the all-slots-free gate are UNCHANGED by this item (see the separate per-slot-identity / tier-aware dispatch work for that).
- Related: LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39 (per-slot identity) would let a future `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots: N` dispatch into partial-idle states; this item only tightens timing, not the slot gate.
data.title: Lower downtimeIdleThresholdMs 240s -> ~60s (plus downtimePollIntervalMs 30s -> 10s floor)

# Herdr downtime dispatcher: scheduled prompts (best-effort frequency)

## Problem statement

The Herdr downtime dispatcher only ever dispatches worklog-derived work (audit → implement → plan → intake tiers). There is no mechanism for periodic, project-scoped prompts (e.g. `/skill:refactor`) to run during downtime on a best-effort cadence, so recurring maintenance must be triggered manually.

## Users

- Operators running the Herdr downtime worker who want recurring maintenance prompts executed automatically during local-LLM idle time.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want `/skill:refactor` to run automatically at least every three days during downtime so the codebase stays clean without manual intervention.
- As an operator, I want scheduled prompts stored in a config file carrying each prompt's desired frequency and last-triggered datetime so I can add, remove, or adjust entries without code changes.
- As an operator, I want a scheduled prompt to dispatch only when the downtime dispatcher actually has a free LLM slot, so maintenance never interrupts active work.
- As an operator, I want scheduled prompts held during a code freeze so no new code changes land mid-release.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl init` provisions a project-local config file `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` containing the base set of scheduled commands — starting with a single `/skill:refactor` entry (`intervalDays: 3`, `lastTriggeredAt: null`) — via a default config template (e.g. `templates/scheduled-prompts.json`). Provisioning is create-if-absent: re-running `wl init` never clobbers an existing file (user edits and `lastTriggeredAt` state are preserved).
2. The config file holds a list of scheduled prompts; each entry has a stable id, the prompt text (any text the pi agent pane can run, e.g. `/skill:refactor`), a best-effort frequency in days (`intervalDays`), and `lastTriggeredAt` (ISO-8601 UTC datetime; `null` = never run). When the file is absent (e.g. a worklog root created before this feature) the worker treats the set as empty: no scheduled dispatch, a logged notice, and existing tiers unaffected (fail-closed; `wl init` is the provisioning path). Malformed files also fail closed: no scheduled dispatch, error logged, existing tiers unaffected.
3. The downtime dispatch pipeline checks scheduled prompts FIRST (before the audit/implement/plan/intake tiers): when an LLM slot is idle and the threshold is met, an entry is due iff `lastTriggeredAt` is null or `now - lastTriggeredAt >= intervalDays` (best effort — a delayed dispatch never fires more often than the frequency). A due entry dispatches a pi agent pane through the existing spawn path (`send-to-pi.sh`, `--pane-name Downtime <id>`, `--no-focus`, `--cwd <wlRoot>`, `--model <downtimeModel>`) running the prompt text.
4. On successful spawn of a scheduled prompt: `lastTriggeredAt` is updated to `now` and persisted to the config file (atomic tmp+rename write), and the dispatch is recorded in `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` with kind `scheduled` (no work-item comment/claim — there is no item). Fail-closed: if the config update or the log-marker write fails, the spawn ABORTS (an unrecorded dispatch never runs) and the entry remains due for the next idle slot.
5. Code-freeze gate applies to scheduled prompts exactly as to the audit/implement tiers: while the marker is frozen or ambiguous (fail-closed), scheduled prompts are skipped and dispatch falls through to the plan/intake tiers (unchanged existing behaviour).
6. When no scheduled prompt is due, the existing tier pipeline runs unchanged (audit → implement → plan → intake). A due scheduled prompt dispatches instead of reaching the backlog tiers, so it never triggers the no-candidate cooldown; when no prompt is due and the backlog is genuinely empty, the existing no-candidate cooldown applies unchanged.
7. Config entries with invalid `intervalDays` (missing, non-finite, or ≤ 0) or missing/empty prompt text are skipped with a logged warning (fail-closed, never a crash); entries missing `lastTriggeredAt` are treated as due. When multiple entries are due, they dispatch one per idle slot in config order.
8. Unit/integration tests cover: `wl init` provisioning (file created with the base set on first init; untouched on re-init), due-check arithmetic (null lastTriggeredAt, boundary, not-yet-due), config parse/defaults/atomic-write, absent/malformed-config fail-closed, freeze gating, cooldown interaction, spawn args, and the `scheduled` log-marker record.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `packages/herdr/README.md`, `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md`, `CONFIG.md` downtime sections).
10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Follow the worker's existing fail-closed philosophy at every boundary: never dispatch, never throw.
- Scheduled check is the first tier of `dispatchDowntimeWork`, gated by the same fresh-read code-freeze marker as audit/implement.
- Per-process single-flight guard (`dispatchInFlight`) applies to scheduled dispatch too — one dispatch per idle slot.
- Reuse the existing scheduler-loop wiring (`createDowntimeWorker.tick`); no new timer infrastructure.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier pipeline (freeze gate → audit → implement → plan → intake), `buildDowntimePrompt`/`buildDowntimePaneArgs`, `DowntimeWorkerDeps` injectable boundary, no-candidate cooldown + three-strike rule in `createDowntimeWorker.tick`, settings clamps.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wires deps (`getNextItem`, `getNextAuditCandidate`, `getNextImplementCandidate`, `readCodeFreezeStatus`, `claimItem`, `spawnAgentPane`, `recordDispatch`, `recordError`).
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — JSON-file settings store pattern (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`), defaults-merge + clamp pattern to mirror.
- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` — rolling dispatch markers (kind `plan|intake|audit|implement`).
- Code-freeze marker: `.worklog/code-freeze.json` (WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY).

## Desired change

Add a scheduled-prompts tier as the first dispatch stage, provisioned by `wl init`. CLI side: `src/commands/init.ts` copies a default config template (new `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` with the `/skill:refactor` base set) into `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` when absent (create-if-absent, never clobber). Plugin side: new module `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` (config load/save/due-check, mirroring `settings.ts` patterns); extend `DowntimeWorkerDeps` with `getDueScheduledPrompt(cwd)` (or equivalent) and reuse `recordDispatch` with kind `scheduled` + a `ScheduledPrompt` event shape; add `dispatchScheduledPrompt` beside `dispatchClaimedTier` (update+persist lastTriggeredAt → log-marker → spawn, abort before spawn on failure); insert the tier in `dispatchDowntimeWork` under the freeze gate. Wire the fs-backed deps in `index.ts`.

## Key Files

- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (new) — default config template: base set with the `/skill:refactor` entry (`intervalDays: 3`, `lastTriggeredAt: null`).
- `src/commands/init.ts` — provision `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` from the template, create-if-absent (never clobber); `src/commands/init.test.ts` (or existing init tests) for provisioning + no-clobber.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` (new) — config schema, load (absent ⇒ empty set, fail-closed), atomic save, due-check (`isDueScheduledPrompt` / `getDueScheduledPrompt`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `ScheduledPrompt` types, `DowntimeDispatchEvent`/`DowntimeDispatchOutcome` kind `scheduled`, `dispatchScheduledPrompt`, tier insertion in `dispatchDowntimeWork`, deps additions.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wire fs-backed scheduled-prompt deps (read config, persist lastTriggeredAt, rolling-log record).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (+ new `scheduled-prompts.test.ts`) — due-check, config, freeze, cooldown, spawn-arg, log-marker tests.
- `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — runtime per-worklog-root config (created by `wl init`, then updated in place by the worker; not committed).
- Docs: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md`, `CONFIG.md` — document the config file, `wl init` provisioning, frequency semantics, and freeze behaviour.

## Related work

- WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B — *Add periodic request scheduling to pi worklog plugin* (completed): cron-based scheduling in the pi extension (`ctx.isIdle()` + `pi.sendUserMessage()`); related pattern, different plugin — reuse the "any prompt text" lesson, not the cron model.
- WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K — *Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime*: parent of the downtime worker.
- WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY — code-freeze gate (freeze semantics reused here).
- WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX — no-candidate cooldown (interaction confirmed in AC5).
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 — implement tier (tier ordering).
- WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — dispatch logging (rolling `.worklog` log + item comments; `scheduled` entries are log-only).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the provisioning path for the config file is `wl init` (the standard worklog-root setup command); the plugin treats an absent file as an empty set (fail-closed, logged) rather than synthesizing defaults.
- **Assumption:** frequency granularity is whole days (`intervalDays`); "every three days" = 72 h. Best-effort means a dispatch may be delayed (no idle slot, cooldown, freeze) but never happens more often than the frequency.
- **Assumption:** multiple due entries dispatch one per idle slot in config order; the single-flight guard prevents overlap.
- **Risk:** concurrent user edit vs worker write of the config file (last-writer-wins) — mitigated by atomic tmp+rename writes and re-reading before each persist.
- **Risk:** clock skew/stale `lastTriggeredAt` makes an entry appear immediately due — acceptable (best-effort), documented.
- **Risk:** `/skill:refactor` runs while the operator is actively working — mitigated: dispatch only happens when an LLM slot is actually idle for the full threshold, unchanged from existing behaviour.
- **Scope creep:** cron-style schedules, per-prompt model overrides, TUI editing of prompts, per-project prompt defaults beyond refactor — record as separate linked work items, not this scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Where should the scheduled-prompts config file live?" — Answer (user/rgardler): "as recommended" — project-local `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, scoping prompts per worklog root (the dispatcher's `cwd`). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "During a code freeze (ship-it marker), should due scheduled prompts still dispatch?" — Answer (user/rgardler): "not during a code-freeze" — scheduled prompts are held by the same freeze gate as the audit/implement tiers (frozen OR ambiguous ⇒ skip; plan/intake still run). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Should a due scheduled prompt bypass the empty-backlog no-candidate cooldown?" — Answer (user/rgardler): "confirmed" — the scheduled check is the first dispatch tier, so a due prompt dispatches instead of reaching the backlog tiers and never triggers the cooldown; when none are due, existing backlog + cooldown behaviour is unchanged. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Requirement (user/rgardler, mid-draft directive): "Add a requirement that wl init will add a base set of scheduled commands, starting with just /skill:refactor (provide a default config file for this purpose)" — Answer: accepted verbatim; `wl init` provisions `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` from a `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` default (base set = `/skill:refactor`, `intervalDays: 3`, `lastTriggeredAt: null`), create-if-absent, never clobbering user edits or `lastTriggeredAt` state. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

# Intake Draft: Downtime dispatcher — priority-first selection with round-robin tie-break across tied items + jittered probes

## Problem statement

When multiple instances of the herdr plugin are active on the same machine, the same instance often wins the race to dispatch in downtime — with a deterministic ascending-sortIndex tie-break, the same lowest-sortIndex item is always picked first by whichever instance is fastest, so one instance monopolises dispatch and tied-priority items are never rotated. Probes also fire in lockstep (all instances at the same fixed poll interval), which amplifies the same-winner effect and gives other machines no chance to get into the loop.

## Users

- **Operator with several herdr panes/instances on one machine** — wants the downtime work spread fairly: highest-priority items first, tied-priority items rotated round-robin, and no single instance hogs all dispatches.
- **Operator with multiple machines sharing the llama proxy** — wants probes desynchronised so each machine gets a fair chance to dispatch first.

### User stories

- As an operator running N herdr instances on one machine, when multiple candidates tie on priority, I want them dispatched in round-robin rotation (shared across instances) so no single item/instance dominates.
- As an operator with several machines on the proxy, I want each downtime probe delayed by a random amount (within ±50% of the poll interval) so instances do not probe in lockstep and other machines can win the dispatch race.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Priority-first selection is preserved: a higher-priority candidate is always selected before any lower-priority candidate, regardless of round-robin state (all tiers: audit, implement, plan/intake).
- [ ] Round-robin tie-break: among candidates sharing the same priority level, selection rotates through them using a shared, durable cursor persisted under `<cwd>/.worklog/` (e.g. `downtime-round-robin.json`), so repeated dispatches of a tied group do not always pick the same item; two instances selecting from the same group pick different items when the cursor has advanced. Unit tests cover rotation across repeated selections and across the three tier selectors.
- [ ] Shared state is fail-open and never blocks dispatch: a missing, unreadable, or corrupt round-robin file degrades to default (no rotation) behaviour; the cursor write failure is tolerated (marker/log write ordering unchanged — the dispatched-marker remains the authoritative guard against re-dispatch).
- [ ] Probe jitter: the downtime task's effective poll interval is jittered ±50% of the configured `downtimePollIntervalMs` per tick (random, injectable RNG for deterministic tests); two workers with identical configuration do not probe in lockstep. Jitter range is verified by unit tests (min/max bounds).
- [ ] Absorbs WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6 (Stagger herdr plugin downtime checks) — the jitter subsumes the stagger intent; that item is marked absorbed/blocked-by this item.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Round-robin grouping key is the **priority level** (critical/high/medium/low), not sortIndex (operator answer).
- Coordination state lives in the existing shared `.worklog/` files — no new daemons, no DB schema change.
- Jitter range is exactly ±50% of the configured poll interval (operator answer).
- Fail-closed / fail-open conventions preserved at every boundary (existing design doctrine); round-robin must never weaken the existing dispatched-marker exclusion or the CAS claim.
- No scope creep: no changes to `wl` CLI selection order (`src/commands`), the Pi TUI mirror, or the grouping/fetcher list ordering.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) runs tiers in order: audit → implement → plan (`intake_complete`) → intake (`idea`).
- Selection (`selectNextCandidate` / `selectAuditCandidate` / `selectImplementCandidate`) sorts candidates ascending by `sortIndex` and picks the first — deterministic, so a tied group always resolves to the same item; the fastest instance wins the CAS claim every time.
- Scheduler (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) registers a fixed-interval `downtime` task (`intervalMs = downtimePollIntervalMs`, default 30s); all instances poll in lockstep.
- Dispatch markers (`downtime-dispatches.log`) + CAS claim (WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN) prevent double-dispatch of the same item but do not address "same instance always wins" or tied-item rotation.

## Desired change

1. **Shared round-robin registry** (`<cwd>/.worklog/downtime-round-robin.json`): map priority level → last-dispatched item id (or rotation cursor). New read/write helpers alongside `downtime-log.ts` (same fail-open discipline). Selection consults the registry: among same-priority candidates, pick the item after the cursor; record the pick before dispatch (write-then-spawn ordering, mirroring the dispatched-marker discipline).
2. **Jittered probes**: the downtime scheduler task's effective interval = `downtimePollIntervalMs + uniform(-50%..+50%)` per tick (injectable RNG; deterministic tests). This absorbs the stagger intent of WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — round-robin selection logic (`selectNextCandidate`, `selectAuditCandidate`, `selectImplementCandidate` gain a rotation-aware variant or shared helper); jitter helper.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — new `downtime-round-robin.json` read/write helpers (mirror existing dispatch-log helpers).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — downtime scheduler task uses jittered interval per tick.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wire rotation registry path into `createDowntimeDeps`/`createDowntimeWorker` (cwd-scoped).
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — only if the interval-mutation approach needs a small hook (prefer mutating the task's `intervalMs` inside its run, which the scheduler already re-reads at reschedule time).
- Tests: `downtime-worker.test.ts`, `downtime-log.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts` / `scheduler.test.ts`.

## Related work

- WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6 — Stagger herdr plugin downtime checks (open, medium): **absorbed by this item** (probe jitter supersedes).
- WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN — Downtime dispatcher: conditional claim + marker exclusion (completed): the CAS/claim infra this builds on; round-robin must compose with it.
- WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (completed): context for the marker/CAS design points.
- WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — Log herdr downtime dispatches (completed): the `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` pattern reused for the round-robin file.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** round-robin rotates *items within a priority level* and is shared across instances on one machine via the local `.worklog/` file; cross-machine fairness relies on jitter + the existing CAS claim (no cross-machine shared state) — consistent with operator answers.
- **Risk:** cursor-write races between instances on the same file. Mitigation: reuse the existing flock/atomic-rename pattern used by the dispatch log; a lost update degrades to a repeated pick, never a wrong-priority pick.
- **Risk:** jitter delays dispatch by up to +50% of the poll interval when a machine would otherwise be first. Accepted per operator instruction (fairness over latency).
- **Risk (scope creep):** do not extend round-robin into `wl` CLI ordering or list rendering; tie-break is a herdr-client concern. Extra opportunities (e.g. cross-machine leases) are recorded as linked work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Round-robin scope — across instances (competing herdr instances take turns) or across items (tied-priority items dispatched in rotation)?" — Answer (user): "(b) across items — when several items tie on priority, they get dispatched in rotation." Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-14.
- Q2: "Coordination mechanism — shared state in `.worklog/` or purely instance-local probabilistic?" — Answer (user): "existing is fine" (shared `.worklog/` files acceptable). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Random delay bounds — range and placement (between probes only, or also pre-dispatch backoff)?" — Answer (user): "±50% of the poll interval" (between probes). Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Tie definition — same priority level regardless of sortIndex, or identical sortIndex?" — Answer (user): "(a) same priority level (critical/high/medium/low)". Source: interactive reply.
- Q5: "Rotation state scope — shared (one rotation per priority group in `.worklog/`) or per-instance?" — Answer (user): "(a) shared — all instances on the machine rotate together". Source: interactive reply.
- Q6: "Relationship to existing stagger item WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6?" — Answer (user): "absorb". Source: interactive reply.

# Refactor Downtime Dispatcher: leader election with shared coordination file

## Problem statement

The current Downtime Dispatcher has every herdr plugin instance polling the llama-proxy independently, using priority, round-robin, and jitter to share dispatch load. This approach still allows one instance to dominate dispatches and doesn't scale well when many instances are active. A leader-election model with a shared coordination file would simplify the dispatch logic: all instances contribute their most important work item to a shared list, one elected leader dispatches work from that list, and the coordination file acts as the single source of truth.

## Users

- **Operator running multiple herdr instances** — wants fair dispatch distribution without per-instance polling complexity; each instance contributes its worklog's most important item to a shared queue.
- **Operator with idle local LLM** — wants work dispatched efficiently: the leader polls for idle slots and pulls from the coordination list, removing dispatched items so others can re-queue.

### User stories

- As an operator running N herdr instances, each instance should automatically join a shared coordination list with its most important work item from its own worklog, identified by instance and worklog directory.
- As an operator, I want one elected leader to handle all LLM idle checks and dispatches, so the other instances don't waste cycles polling the proxy.
- As an operator, if the leader crashes, another instance should automatically take over within 5 minutes.
- As an operator, when the leader dispatches an item, that item is removed from the coordination list and the instance that owned it will add a new item on its next 30-minute check-in.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Leader election** — Instances use a file lock to elect a single leader; the first instance to acquire the lock wins. If no leader is elected (lock unavailable), the instance continues operating without dispatching.
2. **Lease-based leadership** — The leader holds a 5-minute lease, refreshed every time it polls the llama-proxy. If the lease expires (leader crashed or idle), instances detect the expiry and run a new election.
3. **Coordination file** — A shared JSON file at `<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.json` stores one entry per instance: `{instanceId, workItemId, directory, assignedAt, lastUpdated}`. Each instance:
   - On startup and every 30 minutes, reads the coordination file
   - If it has an entry, verifies its work item is still its most important; if not, updates the entry
   - If no entry exists, adds its most important item to the list
   - If its entry was removed (by leader dispatch), adds a new entry on the next check-in
4. **Leader dispatch logic** — The leader reads the coordination file, determines priority order (audit tier first, then implement, then plan, then intake), checks LLM idle status (dispatch poll interval 10s + continuous idle threshold 60s — producer-accepted defaults, see work-item comment 2026-08-24; the 30s proxy status refresh is unchanged), and dispatches the highest-priority available item when a slot opens. The dispatched item is removed from the coordination file.
5. **Multi-worklog support** — Each instance operates on its own worklog directory (identified in the coordination file). The leader compares work items across directories using the standard tier priority system.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Single-machine only for v1** — coordination file access uses flock; no cross-machine support in this version.
- **30-minute check-in interval** — instances update the coordination file every 30 minutes (first check-in on startup).
- **5-minute lease** — leader lease timeout is 5 minutes, refreshed on each proxy poll cycle.
- **Fail-safe** — missing/unreadable coordination file or failed leader election degrades to current behavior (no dispatch from that instance).
- **Existing dispatch guard preserved** — the dispatched-marker exclusion and CAS claim mechanisms continue to prevent double-dispatch.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` runs tiers in order: audit → implement → plan → intake.
- Each herdr instance polls the llama-proxy independently using fixed jittered intervals.
- Dispatch markers (`downtime-dispatches.log`) + CAS claim prevent double-dispatch.
- Coordination file concept doesn't exist; all state is instance-local.
- Key files: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts`.

## Desired change

1. **Leader election module** — New file (`leader-election.ts`) implementing file-lock-based leader election with lease management. Leader refreshes lease on each proxy poll; lease expiry triggers re-election.
2. **Coordination file module** — New file (`coordination.ts`) managing the shared coordination JSON file. Each instance reads/writes its entry; entries contain instanceId, workItemId, worklog directory, and timestamps.
3. **Refactored dispatch worker** — Leader-only dispatch logic reads the coordination file, applies tier priority, checks LLM idle, dispatches the highest-priority item, and removes it. Non-leader instances skip proxy polling and dispatch; they only update their coordination entry on the 30-minute check-in.
4. **Updated scheduler** — Non-leader instances use a 30-minute check-in timer for coordination updates; the leader uses the existing proxy-poll cadence (30s) for LLM idle checks plus coordination updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` — NEW: File-lock leader election with lease management (TTL, expiry detection, re-election).
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — NEW: Shared coordination file read/write (flock, JSON format, entry management).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Refactored: leader checks before dispatch, coordination file integration, tier priority from list.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — May need minor updates to record coordination-file operations alongside dispatches.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Updated: scheduler wiring for leader vs. non-leader timers.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — May need updates for the 30-minute check-in cadence on non-leader instances.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Wire coordination file path and leader election into `createDowntimeDeps`.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6** — Downtime dispatcher: priority-first selection with round-robin tie-break (open) — this refactoring **supersedes** the round-robin/jitter approach; that work item should be closed or marked absorbed. This relationship should be recorded as a blocker/absorbed link.
- **WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN** — Downtime dispatcher: conditional claim + plan/intake marker exclusion (completed) — CAS/claim infrastructure this builds on.
- **WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8** — Log herdr downtime dispatches (completed) — dispatch log pattern reused.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** Each instance operates on its own worklog directory, so "most important item" is computed independently per instance using the standard tier priority.
- **Assumption:** The coordination file is stored in a shared `.worklog/` directory accessible to all instances (local filesystem, not network storage in v1).
- **Risk:** Race conditions during coordination file writes (two instances updating simultaneously). Mitigation: flock on write; brief lock-hold (read-modify-write is fast JSON manipulation).
- **Risk:** Leader election race when multiple instances start simultaneously. Mitigation: file lock is atomic; one wins, others detect lock held and retry after a short backoff (e.g., 1-2 seconds).
- **Risk:** Stale entries from crashed instances linger in the coordination file until they expire or are cleaned up. Mitigation: include `lastUpdated` timestamp per entry; the leader can prune entries older than the lease timeout (5 min) on each dispatch cycle.
- **Risk:** Instance's worklog becomes inaccessible during a check-in (disk error, permission change). Mitigation: fail-open — skip the check-in for that instance, do not remove the entry, log the error.
- **Risk (scope creep):** Ensure the refactoring doesn't inadvertently break existing dispatch guard mechanisms (CAS claim, dispatched-marker exclusion). Extra opportunities (e.g., cross-machine support) are recorded as linked work items, not scope.
- **Risk:** 5-minute lease means up to 5 minutes of no dispatch if leader crashes. Acceptable for v1; could be reduced in a follow-up.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Leader election mechanism?" — Answer (user): "(a) Simple: first to acquire a file lock wins". Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Coordination file contents?" — Answer (user): "work item ID and the directory in which the .worklog folder can be found". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Leader failure / handoff?" — Answer (user): "(b) Lease-based: leader gets a time-limited lease and must re-acquire it periodically". Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Multi-tier scheduling on leader?" — Answer (user): "if an audit tier work item exists, use that; if not check for an implement item; if none try a plan etc." Source: interactive reply.
- Q5: "LLM idle checking?" — Answer (user): "(a) Leader still checks LLM idle status before dispatching (current behavior)". Source: interactive reply.
- Q6: "Multi-machine support?" — Answer (user): "not supported in first version; flock is OK". Source: interactive reply.
- Q7: "Lease duration?" — Answer (user): "5 minutes, refreshed every time the leader polls the proxy". Source: interactive reply.
- Q8: "Re-queueing after dispatch?" — Answer (user): "yes — when leader dispatches and removes an item, the instance adds its next most important item at the next 30-minute check-in". Source: interactive reply.
- Q9: "Dispatch cadence?" — Answer (user): "same as current: poll proxy every 30s, require ~4 min continuous idle, then dispatch one item and wait for a fresh idle period". Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKVYN4HW1AMQFAV** – Add 'Update' UI to change work-item stage (shortcut: U) (completed)
- **WL-0MSI9FDPI005Z0BV** – Audit-tier downtime dispatch tests (completed)
- **WL-0MSKUG2WW0058A7W** – Evaluate downtime-worker config and silent-failure paths (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-Refactor-Downtime-Dispatcher-WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL.md` — matched: coordination, dispatcher, downtime, elect, election, file, important, instance, instances, items, jitter, key, leader, list, llm, model, polling, polls, priority, refactor, robin, round, running, shared, their, update, work
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: dispatcher, downtime, elect, election, file, idea, instance, instances, items, key, leader, list, llm, model, polling, polls, priority, round, running, shared, their, update, work
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSI4TAT70058921-rename-podcast-editing-tab-to-worklog/packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: downtime, elect, election, file, idea, instance, instances, items, key, leader, list, llm, model, polling, polls, priority, round, running, shared, their, update, work

# Exclude child items from audit-tier dispatch selection

## Problem statement

The audit-tier dispatch selects items from `completed` / `in_review` work items without a valid audit, but currently includes child items (sub-tasks) alongside parent items. Child items should never be dispatched independently — only parent items should appear in the audit dispatch tier.

## Users

- **Producers reviewing epics** — the completed/in_review review queue should contain parent items only, so the audit dispatch focuses on reviewing actual deliverable units, not sub-tasks.
- **Downtime dispatcher** — when dispatching `/skill:audit` during idle time, it should only spawn audits for parent items, never for children.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` uses `--root-only` on the `wl list` call so that only items without a parent are returned as audit candidates.
2. All existing audit-tier tests pass with the change (candidates should be unaffected unless they are children, which should now be excluded).
3. If a test or scenario creates child items in `completed`/`in_review`, those children are never returned as audit candidates.
4. Documentation updated: code comments in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` reflecting the root-only constraint; README downtime section updated.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- This is a minimal surgical change: only the `wl list` arguments in `getNextAuditCandidate` need modification (add `--root-only`).
- No changes to the implement-tier selection are in scope — that tier uses `wl next`, which already respects parent-child hierarchy (per completed items WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1 and WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR).

## Existing state

- `getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` calls:
  ```
  wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json
  ```
- `wl list` supports a `--root-only` flag that shows only items without a parent.
- Parent-child hierarchy was already addressed in `wl list` (WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR) and `wl next` (WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1, WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1).

## Desired change

Add `--root-only` to the `wl list` call in `getNextAuditCandidate`:
```
wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json
```

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getNextAuditCandidate` function (line ~405): add `--root-only` to `buildWlArgs` call.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — interface doc comment for `getNextAuditCandidate` may need updating to reflect root-only contract.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — audit selection tests may need a test confirming children are excluded.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — downtime section (update if documenting selection rules).

## Related work

- **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** — Hide child work items from top-level selection lists (Pi and Herdr) — introduces `--root-only` flag on `wl list`.
- **WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1** — wl next should return parent items instead of surfacing children individually — ensures `wl next` returns parents, not children.
- **WL-0MSI9WPNI0044RL8** — Audit dispatch tier — establishes the audit tier concept.
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** — Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit — audit tier wiring.
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY** — Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions — parent for audit-tier dispatched-marker exclusion.
- **WL-0MSLUASNF001LLAT** — Dispatched-marker exclusion in audit-tier selection — child of above.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** If existing tests create child items in `completed`/`in_review`, they were previously valid candidates and now will be excluded — test fixtures may need updating to use root items.
- **Risk:** If ALL `completed`/`in_review` items happen to be children (extremely rare), the audit tier returns no candidates — this is the correct behavior (no root items to audit).
- **Assumption:** `--root-only` does not change the JSON output shape — verified against `wl list --help` (it is a filter flag, not a format modifier).

# parseLlamaStatus rejects numeric slot_id from proxy — all polls fail → never dispatches

## Root Cause

`parseLlamaStatus()` in `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` validates the `slot_id` field with:

```ts
if (typeof slot.slot_id !== 'string' || slot.slot_id.length === 0) return null;
```

but the proxy (`llama-proxy`, `observability.py`) serves `slot_id` as an **integer** (from llama-server's `/slots` `id` field):

```py
"slot_id": slot.get("id", i)   # int
```

## Impact

Every 30-second poll → `parseLlamaStatus` returns `null` → fail-closed "busy" → the 4-minute continuous-idle dispatch gate can never be met. The plugin UI shows `[downtime busy]` even during verified idle windows.

## Reproduction (live, confirmed)

```
payload.slots = [{"slot_id":0,"is_processing":true,...},{"slot_id":1,...},{"slot_id":2,...}]
>>> PARSE FAILS: slot_id is number (0), parser requires string
worker verdict: parseLlamaStatus returns null -> treated as BUSY (fail-closed)
```

## Timeline

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Aug 13 15:50 | Worker's strict string-`slot_id` parser landed (`ea25eab1`) |
| Aug 14 11:25 | Proxy started serving `slots` with **int** `slot_id` (`c9f69c3`, deployed 11:38) |
| Aug 14→15 | Old plugin pane (pre-Aug-13 code, ignored `slots` field) kept dispatching — last dispatch Aug 15 16:35:55Z |
| Aug 15 17:40 local | Plugin restarted → **new instance loads strict parser** → every poll fails → zero dispatches from then on |

## Fix

- Make `parseLlamaStatus` accept numeric `slot_id` (coerce `Number`→string) — the proxy contract is int
- Add regression test with numeric `slot_id` (mirroring the live payload)
- After fix, restart the plugin pane; the next ≥4-min idle window should dispatch again

## Test

Add a test in `downtime-worker.test.ts`:

```ts
it('accepts numeric slot_id (proxy contract)', () => {
  const status = parseLlamaStatus({
    llama_server_running: true,
    active_query: false,
    model_switch_in_progress: false,
    available_slots: 3,
    total_slots: 3,
    slots: [{slot_id: 0, is_processing: false}],
  });
  expect(status).not.toBeNull();
});
```
data.title: Downtime worker: parseLlamaStatus rejects numeric slot_id — every poll fail-closes to busy, zero dispatches

## Summary

Audit reports with `Ready to close: Yes` are being persisted without the required status/stage lifecycle transition (`completed`/`in_review`), leaving items stranded in `idea`/`open` despite passing audits.

## Discovery

3 idea-stage items had passing audits (`Ready to close: Yes`) but remained `status=open` / `stage=idea`:

- WL-0MSGRJWRX0068W3W — audited 2026-08-10, still idea/open until manually fixed 2026-08-16
- WL-0MSHUMX5C004NC4O — audited 2026-08-11, still idea/open until manually fixed 2026-08-16
- WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6 — audited 2026-08-10, still idea/open until manually fixed 2026-08-16

All three had identical `updatedAt` (2026-08-16T12:49:59) — 5-6 days after their audits — indicating the lifecycle update never ran or was silently reverted/bulk-touched afterward.

## Root cause hypothesis

The audit skill's runner (`audit_runner.py`) persists the audit report and then attempts the lifecycle update via `wl update --status completed --stage in_review`, but the skill documentation explicitly states: **"status-update failures are silently caught (still reported)"**. There is no post-update verification that the status/stage actually changed. Alternative path: manual `wl audit-set` (or `wl create --audit-text`) persists the report with NO lifecycle at all.

## Expected behaviour

- After an audit with `Ready to close: Yes`, the item MUST end in `status=completed` / `stage=in_review` (or terminal `done`).
- After `Ready to close: No`, the item MUST end in `status=open` / `stage=plan_complete`.
- On failure/timeout, the item MUST be restored to its pre-audit status/stage.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After the audit runner persists a `Yes` verdict, it verifies the item's status/stage actually transitioned to `completed`/`in_review` (via `wl show <id> --json` readback); if not, it retries and/or exits non-zero with a clear diagnostic — never a silent success.
- [ ] The same verification applies to `No` verdicts (`open`/`plan_complete`) and the failure-restore path (pre-audit status/stage).
- [ ] A passing audit can never leave an item in `idea`/`open` without a visible, operator-visible error.
- [ ] Regression test: simulate a failing/silently-swallowed `wl update` (or audit-set without lifecycle) and assert the runner reports the failure instead of exiting 0.

# Shared round-robin registry + rotation-aware selection

## Summary

Implement the shared, durable round-robin cursor for downtime dispatch.

## Implementation

- File: `.worklog/downtime-round-robin.json` in the worklog directory
- Schema: `{ cursor: number, version: number }` — cursor advances on each dispatch
- All operations are fail-open: missing file, unreadable file, or corrupt JSON → default to no rotation (cursor=0)
- Write operations use atomic rename (write to temp → rename) to prevent partial reads
- Thread-safe for herdr plugin use (file-based, not in-memory)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `loadCursor()` returns the cursor value (number), defaulting to `0` when the file does not exist
- [x] `loadCursor()` returns the persisted cursor value for valid file content (`version` is tracked internally in the file schema)
- [x] `loadCursor()` returns default (0) on corrupt JSON (no exception thrown)
- [x] Cursor persistence uses atomic write (temp + rename); the write is internal to `advanceCursor()` via `saveRoundRobinFile()`
- [x] `advanceCursor(tier, groupSize)` returns the selected index (`cursor % groupSize`) and saves it; handles per-tier priority group rotation
- [x] Concurrent cursor writes cannot corrupt the file (atomic tmp+rename → last write wins; version increments per advance)
- [x] No new dependencies added (pure file I/O, no external libraries)

# Dispatch wiring (write-then-spawn cursor) + jittered probes

## Summary

Wire the round-robin registry into the dispatch flow end-to-end: read and advance the rotation cursor before each dispatch (write-then-spawn), and add jitter to the probe interval.

## Implementation

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` in `downtime-worker.ts` reads the round-robin cursor BEFORE spawning dispatch
- Cursor is advanced atomically before dispatch spawns
- Probe interval: `downtimePollIntervalMs * (1 + jitter)` where jitter ∈ [-0.5, +0.5]
- Jitter is calculated per-tick (not cached across ticks) so instances desynchronize
- RNG is injectable (mockable) for deterministic tests

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Dispatch flow reads round-robin cursor, selects candidate, advances cursor (write-then-spawn), THEN spawns dispatch
- [x] Jitter is applied to each probe interval independently (not cached)
- [x] Jitter bounds verified: effective interval ∈ [0.5*pollInterval, 1.5*pollInterval]
- [x] Two workers with same poll interval produce different probe times within one minute (jitter desync)
- [x] Cursor is advanced at SELECTION time (write-then-spawn ordering, per the child title) — before the spawn outcome is known; the dispatched-marker exclusion + CAS claim prevent re-dispatch of the same item, so the rotation remains correct even when a spawn subsequently fails
- [x] Existing dispatched-marker exclusion still works (no regression)
- [x] No changes to `wl` CLI, Pi TUI, or grouping/fetcher list ordering

# Enable cut and paste in the herdr command-input page (form fields)

## Problem Statement

The herdr plugin's command-input form page — opened by **any** chord whose command template contains unknown `<identifier>` fields (e.g. `P p` prompt, `c` create, `u t` title, `n e` note edit) — accepts only single printable keypresses. Pasting from the OS clipboard is unreliable: bracketed-paste control sequences are mangled and any newline in pasted text immediately submits the form. There is no way to cut or copy field text to the OS clipboard, and multi-line field values are impossible.

## Users

Daily work-item managers and keyboard-driven power users who compose prompts, descriptions, and titles inside herdr command forms.

### Example User Stories

- As a **work-item manager**, I want to press `Ctrl+V` in the `<description>` field of the `c` (create) form to paste a bug report from my notes, so I don't retype it.
- As a **power user**, I want to press `Ctrl+X` on a URL I just typed into the `P p` (prompt) field and paste it elsewhere, so my clipboard stays usable.
- As a **note editor**, I want to paste multi-line content (or insert blank lines with `Ctrl+Enter`) into a description/field without the form submitting early, so I can compose freely.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Ctrl+V` in the active form field reads the OS clipboard and inserts its contents into the field; pasted text (including `
` / `
` line breaks) is preserved verbatim and does **not** submit the form.
- [ ] `Ctrl+X` on the active field copies the field's full current value to the OS clipboard and clears the field, with visible feedback (hint/toast).
- [ ] `Ctrl+Enter` inserts a newline into the active field while plain `Enter` still submits the form.
- [ ] Bracketed-paste sequences (`\x1b[200~` … `\x1b[201~`) arriving via any paste path (e.g. terminal-level paste) are unwrapped so the inner content is inserted cleanly, with no control-sequence characters and no accidental submit/navigation.
- [ ] Multi-line field values render readably in the full-pane form page (wrapped display, page-height honored, no layout breakage).
- [ ] When no OS clipboard reader is available, paste fails gracefully with a visible message and the form stays open (no crash, no data loss).
- [ ] Testing: unit tests covering paste (single-line/multi-line/bracketed), cut, `Ctrl+Enter`, no-submit-on-pasted-newline, and clipboard helper mocks; **all related documentation is updated** (code comments + plugin/README docs); **the full project test suite passes** with the changes (CHANGELOG.md excluded — managed by the release pipeline).

## Constraints

- **No tmux dependency**: the environment is herdr (not tmux); clipboard operations must target the OS clipboard directly (platform tools / OSC 52), reusing the strategy in `src/clipboard.ts` — no tmux-buffer branch.
- Clipboard reads are async; the TUI must not freeze (non-blocking UX).
- Surgical scope: extend `FormState.handleInput` + rendering and add a clipboard-read helper; no redesign of field editing (values remain appended at the end; no in-field cursor/selection model is added unless trivially required — see Assumptions).
- Command templates stay single-line; pasted newlines are preserved in the displayed/substituted value.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts`: `FormState.handleInput` handles Enter submit, Esc cancel, Tab/arrow field navigation, Backspace delete-last-char, and single printable-char append; everything else is ignored. No paste/cut/newline handling exists. The form renders as a full-pane page layout.
- `src/clipboard.ts`: `copyToClipboard` exists (OSC 52 + platform tools `pbcopy`/`clip`/`wl-copy`/`xclip`/`xsel`, plus a tmux branch). **No OS-clipboard read (paste) helper exists anywhere.**

## Desired change

1. Add an OS-clipboard **read** helper (e.g. `pbpaste` / `clip` via PowerShell `Get-Clipboard` / `wl-paste` / `xclip -o` / `xsel -b`), platform-ordered like `copyToClipboard`, placed in the shared/herdr package boundary so tests can mock it via the existing injectable-seam patterns.
2. Extend `FormState.handleInput` (+ async result plumbing in the input loop): `Ctrl+V` → insert clipboard text into active field; `Ctrl+X` → copy field value to clipboard and clear it; `Ctrl+Enter` → insert `
`; unwrap bracketed-paste sequences as verbatim insertions (newlines are data, never submit).
3. Update the form render to display multi-line values wrapped within the existing page layout, preserving cursor/hint indicators.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — key handling (paste/cut/`Ctrl+Enter`/bracketed-paste unwrap) + multi-line rendering
- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.test.ts` — input-handling unit tests
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` / `worklist.ts` — key routing / async result delivery into form state (wiring for Ctrl chords and async clipboard calls)
- `src/clipboard.ts` (or `packages/shared`) — add clipboard-read helper following the platform-tool strategy

## Risks & Assumptions

- Herdr may deliver keypresses char-by-char, so bracketed-paste unwrapping may need buffered state across `handleInput` calls (pairing `\x1b[200~` … `\x1b[201~`); AC 4 must be validated against herdr's actual key delivery in integration testing.
- Multi-line values substituted into command templates must stay safe for the `wl`/shell command path (argument escaping) — implementation concern, not a UX change.
- Scope-creep guard: in-field selection/cursor editing is out of scope; only whole-field cut is added (see Appendix assumption). If selection-based cut/copy is wanted, that is a separate work item.

## Related Work

- Form input dialog for unknown identifiers in Herdr chord commands (WL-0MS690SJG003H7WK) — the form page this feature extends
- Herdr shortcuts: P-p free prompt and P-a audit-gaps prompt (WL-0MSGHNTMF000YKRI)
- Herdr plugin: creating a new intake (c key) fires up two pi instances (WL-0MSAL0RN1009YNJ7)
- Herdr command input dialog layout fixes (WL-0MSAKRBOC005T320, WL-0MSFZUS4Z006IRI3)
- Clipboard copy strategy items (WL-0MM413YHZ0HTNF4J, WL-0MKYGWIBY19OUL78, WL-0MKX63DHJ101712F, WL-0MMIXP0GC1MMFGNL) — copyToClipboard pattern to reuse/parallel

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Is 'the editor' the command-input form page (the `<prompt>` field for `P-p`, the `<description>`/`<priority>` fields for `c`, etc.), or a different editor in the herdr plugin?" — Answer (user, intake reply): "I mean the command input page, for **all** commands not just the examples provided." Source: interactive reply (session `herdr-1786906600-2481950-22106`).
- Q: "Do you want explicit Ctrl+X/Ctrl+V wired to the OS clipboard (pasteable elsewhere), or just reliable terminal paste?" — Answer (user, intake reply): "wired to OS (note we use Herdr not Tmux)". Source: interactive reply. Research: `src/clipboard.ts` currently targets tmux buffers first when `$TMUX` is set — the herdr path must skip tmux and use OS tools/OSC 52 only.
- Q: "Should pasted multi-line text be preserved or flattened?" — Answer (user, intake reply): "preserved (may need to add support for CTRL-Enter to add a blank line too)". Source: interactive reply. Adds `Ctrl+Enter` newline-insertion requirement (AC 3).
- Assumption (flagged, not confirmed): with no in-field selection model today, "cut" operates on the **entire active-field value** (copy to clipboard + clear field). If selection-based cut is desired this is a scope addition — surfaced for review before implementation.
data.title: Enable cut and paste in the herdr command-input page (all command forms)

## Summary

Add verification that the status/stage actually transitioned after the audit runner persists an audit report.

## Problem

The audit runner calls `wl update --status completed --stage in_review` (or `--status open --stage plan_complete`), but failures are silently caught. Items end up stranded in their pre-audit stage with `Ready to close: Yes` audit reports.

## Implementation

In `scripts/audit_runner.py`, after calling `wl update` to change status/stage:
1. Immediately read back the item state via `wl show <id> --json`
2. Verify the status and stage match expected values:
   - For `Ready to close: Yes` -> `status=completed`, `stage=in_review`
   - For `Ready to close: No` -> `status=open`, `stage=plan_complete`
3. If the verification fails, retry the update up to 3 times with short delays
4. After retries exhausted, exit non-zero with a clear diagnostic message

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/audit_runner.py`

## Deliverables
- Modified audit_runner.py with verification + retry logic
- All existing tests still pass
- New test added (see regression test task)

## Summary

Before attempting the lifecycle update, save the item's current status/stage. If the verification fails after retries, restore the saved state and exit non-zero.

## Implementation

In `scripts/audit_runner.py`:

# Critical: herdr mouse-input test suite fails (41 failures) — tests committed without implementation

## Summary

`packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` fails with **41 failures** in the herdr package vitest run (`npx vitest run packages/herdr`). The test suite imports mouse-handling symbols from `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` that are **not exported/implemented**, so the whole file fails (mostly `is not a function` / `undefined` assertion errors).

Discovered while implementing WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9 (metadata section icons). **Not caused by that change** — the failures predate it and reproduce on the unmodified `dev` branch.

## Evidence

```
npx vitest run packages/herdr
Test Files  1 failed | 33 passed (34)
     Tests  41 failed | 1049 passed (1090)
```

Sample failures:

- `ANSI mouse sequences > defines the exact mouse-tracking enable sequence (1000 + 1002 + 1006)` — `expect(ANSI.mouseEnable).toBe('\x1b[?1000h\x1b[?1002h\x1b[?1006h')` → received `undefined`
- `ANSI mouse sequences > defines the exact mouse-tracking disable sequence (h → l)` — `ANSI.mouseDisable` → `undefined`
- `parseMouseEvent > parses a left press` — `TypeError: parseMouseEvent is not a function`
- … and 38 more (consumeMouseChunk, mapMouseToAction, DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS coverage, etc.)

## Root cause

The test suite is the **TDD red phase** of the mouse/touch feature (parent **WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ** "Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the selection list"):

- Commit `4d7a09e1` — `WL-0MSI720DX002E9WC: Test: mouse input handling suite (TDD red phase)` committed the tests **before the implementation slice was done**.
- The implementation item **WL-0MSI7278X0008XGM** ("Implement: mouse tracking lifecycle + SGR parser") is still **open** — it was supposed to add exactly these symbols.

Missing exports in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (grep confirms):

| Symbol (imported by the test) | Exported in worklist.ts? |
|---|---|
| `ANSI.mouseEnable` / `ANSI.mouseDisable` | ❌ (ANSI object exists, entries absent) |
| `parseMouseEvent` | ❌ |
| `consumeMouseChunk` | ❌ |
| `mapMouseToAction` | ❌ |

| `ParsedMouseEvent`, `MouseAction`, `MouseClickState`, `TermSize` (types) | ❌ |
| `runWorklistTui`, `WorkItemListState`, `handleKeypress`, `keyToAction` | ✅ (existing) |

Because the imports resolve to `undefined`/missing, **all 41 tests in the file fail**, not just the mouse-specific ones.

## Impact

- `packages/herdr` package test suite is **red**: `npx vitest run packages/herdr` fails 41 tests.
- Blocks the "all tests pass" gate for any herdr work item (`test-failure` triage policy).
- The planned fix (WL-0MSI7278X0008XGM) is the correct completion of the feature; until then the suite is polluted and a developer cannot distinguish real regressions from the red-phase noise.

2. **Stopgap:** If mouse support is deferred, the test suite should be marked/removed so the package suite is green again (requires explicit approval — do not auto-remove; the tests are useful and match the planned feature).

## Repro

```bash
cd packages/herdr && npx vitest run packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts
```

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` — failing test file (committed in 4d7a09e1)

# Leader Election Module

## Summary
New `leader-election.ts` implementing file-lock-based leader election with 5-minute lease management and expiry detection.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A file lock at `<worklog-root>/.worklock/downtime-leader.lock` is used to elect a single leader
2. Leader acquires an initial lease (5 min TTL); lease is refreshed on each proxy poll cycle
3. Non-leader instances detect lock held and retry with exponential backoff (1-2s initial)
4. Lease expiry (5 min no refresh) triggers re-election by other instances
5. When coordination file is missing/unreadable, instance degrades gracefully (no dispatch)

## Minimal Implementation
- `flock`-based file lock with TTL tracking
- Lease stored as JSON `{leaderId, acquiredAt, ttlSeconds}`
- `isLeader()` returns boolean; `refreshLease()` updates TTL
- `detectStaleLeader()` checks for expiry and clears stale state

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/tests/leader-election.test.ts` — Unit tests for lock acquisition/expiration/re-election

# Shared Coordination File Module

## Summary
New `coordination.ts` managing the shared coordination JSON file at `<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.json` with per-instance entry management.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Each instance reads/writes its own entry using flock for safe concurrent access
2. Entry format: `{instanceId, workItemId, directory, assignedAt, lastUpdated}`
3. On startup and every 30 minutes, instance verifies its entry matches its most-important item
4. If no entry exists, adds its most-important item from its worklog
5. Leader can prune stale entries (lastUpdated > 5 min) during dispatch cycles

## Minimal Implementation
- `readCoordinationFile()` — reads JSON under flock
- `writeCoordinationFile(data)` — writes JSON under flock
- `upsertEntry(instanceId, worklogDir, workItemId)` — adds or updates instance entry
- `pruneStaleEntries(maxAgeSec)` — removes entries older than threshold
- `getMostImportantItem(worklogDir)` — finds highest-priority item for an instance

## Deliverables

## Summary
Refactored `downtime-worker.ts` where only the leader performs dispatch; non-leader instances skip proxy polling and only do 30-min coordination check-ins.

# Intake Brief: Shortcut key to toggle downtime dispatch per herdr instance

## Problem statement

Herdr's downtime dispatcher (local-LLM idle dispatch) is gated only by the
global `downtimeEnabled` setting in `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`;
there is no quick way to stop or resume dispatch for a single herdr pane.
Because multiple herdr instances (panes/tabs) run concurrently — dispatch is
leader-only (WL-0MSXHA1B0005G3E5) — an operator needs a per-instance control
so they can pause dispatch on one pane (e.g. while working interactively
there) without touching the shared settings file or affecting other panes.

## Users

- **Herdr operators running multiple panes** — want to pause/resume downtime
  dispatch on the current pane with a single keypress, with visible header
  feedback.
  - As an operator, I press `d` in the worklist to immediately stop downtime
    dispatch for this pane, and the header shows `[Downtime Off]`.
  - As an operator, I press `d` again to resume dispatch for this pane; the
    header returns to the live status (`[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]` /
    `[downtime busy]`).
  - As an operator running several herdr panes, toggling one pane does not
    affect the others, and my change is forgotten when the plugin restarts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new `d` chord shortcut (bundled `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`)
   toggles downtime dispatch for the current herdr instance: pressing it
   while enabled disables dispatch for that instance; pressing again
   re-enables it. The shortcut is listed in the bottom help-hints bar with a
   descriptive label.
2. The toggle is **per-instance and in-memory** (user-confirmed scope a):
   other herdr panes are unaffected, the shared settings file is never
   written, and the state resets on plugin restart.
3. The worklist header shows `[Downtime Off]` whenever dispatch is disabled
   for the instance, replacing the current `[downtime disabled]` text (user-
   confirmed). When enabled, the existing status indicators
   (`[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]`, `[downtime busy]`, `[downtime paused]`,
   `[⏳ downtime dispatching]`) are unchanged.
4. While toggled off, the worker performs no proxy polling, idle tracking, or
   dispatch (same behavior as settings-disabled) — `tick()` short-circuits
   exactly like the `!cfg.enabled` path.
5. The toggle is handled as an **internal TUI action** — it must not spawn a
   new pane or write to stdout (routed through `dispatchChordCommand` like
   the `/wl <stage>` family) so the header updates immediately.
6. Unit tests cover: chord routing for the new internal command family (no
   pane dispatch), the worker's per-instance toggle (enabled getter + tick
   early-return), header rendering of `[Downtime Off]`, per-instance
   isolation (two workers toggle independently), and toggling when the
   global setting is disabled.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (README
   downtime-worker section + chord shortcut list, code comments); the full
   project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Per-pane in-memory only** (user answer to Q1: option a). No writes to
  `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`, no per-project marker files, no
  persistence across restarts.
- **Internal action, not a pane dispatch** — the toggle flips in-memory
  worker state and re-renders the header in place.
- **`d` key must not conflict** with existing chords or navigation keys
  (verified: `d` is currently unused as a bare chord; two-key chords like
  `x d` / `n d` are unaffected).
- Reuse the existing `shortcuts.json` → `ShortcutRegistry` → chord-dispatch
  pipeline so help hints, stage gating, and local overrides keep working.
- Keep signature changes backward compatible (new params optional) so
  existing unit tests and callers keep compiling.

## Existing state

- Chords in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` resolve through
  `ShortcutRegistry` (`shortcut-config.ts`) and route via
  `executeResolvedCommand` → `dispatchChordCommand` (`worklist.ts`): the
  `/wl <stage>` family is handled internally; everything else goes to
  `onCommand` (pane dispatch / stdout).
- `createDowntimeWorker` (`downtime-worker.ts`): the `enabled` getter
  re-reads the global settings file every tick via `config()`;
  `tick()` early-returns when `!cfg.enabled`. There is no per-instance
  override today.
- `index.ts` only creates the worker when `runSettings.downtimeEnabled` is
  true — so a toggle cannot currently re-enable dispatch on a pane whose
  global setting is off.
- `renderDowntimeStatus` (`worklist.ts`) renders `[downtime disabled]` when
  `!worker.enabled`; the header otherwise shows `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]`,
  `[downtime busy]`, `[downtime paused]`, `[⏳ downtime dispatching]`.
- Multiple concurrent instances exist (leader-only dispatch,
  WL-0MSXHA1B0005G3E5), each with its own `DowntimeWorker`.

## Desired change

- Add a `d` chord to the bundled `shortcuts.json` with an internal command
  (e.g. `/downtime toggle`), label `downtime toggle`, view `both`.
- Add a per-instance in-memory override to `createDowntimeWorker`
  (`override: boolean | null`, default null = follow settings) plus a
  `toggle()` method; effective enabled = `override ?? cfg.enabled`, honored
  by both the `enabled` getter and `tick()`.
- Create the worker unconditionally in `index.ts` (the override gates it) so
  `d` can also force dispatch on for one pane when the global setting is
  off.
- Recognize the new internal command family in `dispatchChordCommand` /
  `executeResolvedCommand` (thread an optional toggle callback or worker
  reference) and return `'dispatched'` without spawning a pane.
- `renderDowntimeStatus`: replace the `[downtime disabled]` branch with
  `[Downtime Off]`.
- Tests + README updates as listed in the ACs.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — add the `d` chord entry
  (`/downtime toggle`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — per-instance override +
  `toggle()`; effective enabled in the getter and in `tick()`.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — internal handling of the new command
  family in `dispatchChordCommand`/`executeResolvedCommand`; `[Downtime Off]`
  in `renderDowntimeStatus`; thread the toggle into the chord path.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — create the worker unconditionally; pass
  the toggle plumbing through `runWorklistTui` options.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts`
  — unit tests per AC6.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the `d` shortcut and `[Downtime Off]`
  header text.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSXHA1B0005G3E5` — "Implement leader-only dispatch logic". Context:
  multiple herdr instances run concurrently; per-instance semantics of the
  toggle.
- `WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY` — "Downtime dispatcher must honour ship-it code
  freezes". Related: fail-closed dispatch gating the toggle interacts with.
- `WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K` / `WL-0MSG80AG700429M8` — "Downtime settings &
  proxy status poller" / "Idle tracker & dispatch orchestration". Related:
  the `[⏳ downtime idle …]` header status (AC3) and worker lifecycle.
- `WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX` — "downtime paused (no-candidate cooldown)" header
  status; adjacent header-rendering logic in `renderDowntimeStatus`.
- `WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y` — "Herdr pane title should reflect how it was
  spawned". Related: same TUI/dispatch plumbing area.
- `WL-0MQDR4V7O007O7TZ` — "Prevent shortcut keys from hijacking navigation
  keys". Related: chord-selection precedent for choosing a safe key.
- `WL-0MSHUMX5C004NC4O` — project-local `shortcuts.json` overrides; the
  bundled entry must respect the merge mechanism.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (confirm):** the per-instance override takes precedence over
  the global `downtimeEnabled` setting, so `d` can force dispatch on for one
  pane even when the operator disabled it globally. Alternative: override
  only suppresses (toggle-on returns to "follow settings"). Default chosen:
  override precedence (true on/off toggle per instance).
- **Assumption:** `[Downtime Off]` replaces `[downtime disabled]` for *all*
  disabled states (settings-off and toggled-off), per the user's Q2 answer
  ("replace the existing text").
- **Risk:** threading the toggle through `dispatchChordCommand` /
  `executeResolvedCommand` changes exported signatures — keep new params
  optional and update existing unit tests.
- **Risk:** creating the worker unconditionally changes startup slightly
  (worker object exists but tick no-ops while disabled) — ensure no proxy
  polling or idle tracking occurs while the effective state is off.
- **Scope-creep guard:** settings-file persistence, cross-instance
  coordination, and per-project marker files are explicitly out of scope
  (per user answer a); any such ideas discovered during implementation
  should be recorded as linked work items, not folded in.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope of 'that instance' — should the toggle be (a) per-pane
  in-memory (current pane only, resets on restart, other panes unaffected),
  (b) per-pane persistent (marker file under .worklog/), or (c) global
  (flips downtimeEnabled in the shared settings file)?"
  - Answer (user, interactive reply): **a — per-pane in-memory**.
- Q2: "Replace the existing `[downtime disabled]` header text with
  `[Downtime Off]` when off, keeping the existing idle/busy/paused/
  dispatching indicators when on?"
  - Answer (user, interactive reply): **yes**.
- Q3: "Shortcut key — `d` (downtime), `t` (toggle), or other? Should it
  appear in the bottom help-hints bar?"
  - Answer (user, interactive reply): **`d`**; shown as a normal shortcut
    entry (help-hints bar included via the standard shortcuts.json
    pipeline).
data.title: Shortcut key to toggle downtime dispatch per herdr instance

## Summary

Single left-click on a worklist row opens the detail view instead of just moving the selection there (as if Enter was pressed instead of arrow keys).

## Root cause

In `runWorklistTui` → `dispatchMouse` (packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts), the clickState tracker is updated to the CURRENT event BEFORE `mapMouseToAction` runs:

```ts
clickState.lastClick = { x: mouseEvent.x, y: mouseEvent.y, at: Date.now() };
clickState.now = clickState.lastClick.at;
const action = mapMouseToAction(state, mouseEvent, termSize, clickState);
```

`mapMouseToAction` then checks `clickState.lastClick.x === ev.x && clickState.lastClick.y === ev.y && now - lastClick.at <= 400` — the current event always matches itself (delta = 0ms), so EVERY left press is classified as a double-click → `open-detail` (list mode) instead of `select-row`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A single left click/tap on a visible list row moves the selection to that item WITHOUT opening the detail view (parent AC2 behavior restored)

# Herdr worklist pane crashes seconds after opening (`prefix+l`)

## Problem statement

Pressing `prefix+l` (bound to `worklog-selection-list.open-podcast-editor-tab`) opens the worklist TUI pane, which then **exits with code 1 within ~3 seconds**, killing the pane.

## Root cause

`HerdrEventSubscriber.doConnect()` attaches the socket `'error'` handler with `once('error', onError)` and then **removes it** (`removeListener('error', onError)`) once the initial `events.subscribe` succeeds. After that, the socket has no `'error'` listener. When herdr later resets/closes the socket connection, Node emits an **unhandled `'error'` event (`ECONNRESET`)**, which crashes the whole Node process (exit code 1). The `main().catch()` handler in `src/index.ts` calls `process.exit(1)`.

Evidence (server log): pane spawns → `events.subscribe` succeeds → ~2.7s later the socket resets → `pane.exit status="ExitStatus { code: 1 }"`. Pane stderr shows `Error: read ECONNRESET` with an unhandled `'error'` event on the Socket.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: After a successful `events.subscribe`, the subscriber keeps an `'error'` handler on the socket.
- [ ] AC2: A post-subscribe socket reset/error is routed to `handleSocketError` (fail-open reconnect), never an unhandled `'error'` crash.
- [ ] AC3: Regression test covers the post-subscribe error path (test fails without the fix).
- [ ] AC4: Live `herdr plugin pane open` worklist pane survives beyond the previous ~3s crash window.
data.title: Herdr worklist pane crashes with exit code 1 seconds after opening (prefix+l) due to unhandled ECONNRESET

# Herdr: re-enable terminal drag-select while keeping mouse support (WL-0MT0AP2LR000JFWN)

## Problem

When mouse tracking is enabled in the worklist TUI (packages/herdr), the terminal sends ALL mouse events to the app, including drag events. This prevents the terminal's native text selection (click-drag to select/copy content from the terminal). Users cannot select text to copy while the worklist TUI is active, even though the TUI needs mouse support for clicking/wheel navigation.

The root cause is that SGR mouse reporting captures all mouse events from the terminal, preventing the terminal's built-in text-selection mechanism from receiving drag events.

## Root cause location

- packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts line 3541: mouseEnable is emitted on raw-mode entry and stays enabled for the TUI lifetime.
- packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts line 3560: mouseDisable is only emitted in cleanup() (TUI exit).
- Once enabled, ALL mouse events are captured, the terminal has no way to selectively receive drag events for selection.

## Solution

Add a toggle shortcut (Alt+m) that allows the user to temporarily disable mouse tracking, use the terminal's native text selection to copy content, then re-enable mouse tracking for worklist interaction.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Toggle shortcut Alt+m toggles mouse tracking on/off. Verified by unit test on the toggle key handling.
2. Toggle state tracked as boolean (mouseTrackingEnabled), initialized to true (mouse tracking enabled by default). Verified by unit test.
3. Toggle works in all modes: Alt+m is handled in the onData handler BEFORE mode-specific dispatch, so it works in list mode, detail mode, and filter mode.
4. Toggle shortcut shown in footer hints.
5. No regression to existing keyboard shortcuts: Alt+m sequence is handled before falling through to keyToAction, so meta-down (m) is unaffected.
6. All existing tests pass.
7. Documentation updated.

### Constraints

- Alt+m (escape+m) must be consumed before reaching keyToAction so meta-down (m) is unaffected.
- The toggle shortcut must be handled in onData before the modal-state guards so it always works.
- Toggle must emit the correct ANSI sequence (enable/disable) to the terminal.
- The mouseTrackingEnabled state must be initialized to true (mouse tracking on by default).

### Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts: toggle state, toggle handler in onData, footer hint update.
- docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md: add note about mouse toggle shortcut.
- packages/herdr/dist/: rebuild via npm run build.
data.title: Herdr: re-enable terminal drag-select while keeping mouse support
