# Tests: mode-switch worker core

Test-first unit tests for the mode-switch worker core (parent WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9): idle-window evaluation, last-command tracking, cheap/fast switch triggers, restart reset, and fail-closed paths.

## Goal
`packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` covering the pure logic of the new worker so implementation can proceed test-first.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Idle-window evaluation:** test that `lastOperatorCommandAt` null (never set this process) is treated as idle after the threshold; a timestamp older than `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` triggers the cheap path; a fresh timestamp (within threshold) does not.
- [ ] **Last-command tracking:** test that an agent-route command updates `lastOperatorCommandAt` to now.
- [ ] **Cheap switch trigger:** test that idle-window met AND proxy idle (reusing `evaluateIdle` semantics, `requiredFreeSlots = 0`/all slots free) yields a `POST /admin/set-mode {"mode":"cheap"}`; busy proxy (active local query) delays the switch.
- [ ] **Fast switch trigger:** test that a new operator agent-route command yields `POST /admin/set-mode {"mode":"fast"}` fire-and-forget.
- [ ] **No redundant switching:** test that when last-known mode already matches the target, no POST is issued (refresh via `GET /admin/mode` on poll).
- [ ] **Restart reset:** test that worker construction sets `lastOperatorCommandAt = Date.now()` (active now; fail-safe fast).
- [ ] **Fail-closed paths:** test that endpoint failure, timeout, network error, ambiguous response, and `409` (mode-switch restart in progress) yield NO switch and never throw; `409` is a no-op retried later.
- [ ] **Settings clamps:** defaults/floors asserted via the settings contract (ties to the settings test child).
- [ ] All tests pass in the project test suite.

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` (new)
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` (under test)

# Implement: mode-switch worker core

New `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` implementing the activity-gated mode switching decision logic (parent WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9), satisfying the worker-core test child.

## Goal
A worker that tracks `lastOperatorCommandAt`, evaluates the idle window against `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs`, reuses the existing `/llama/local/status` idle evaluation (`evaluateIdle`, all slots free), tracks last-known mode (refreshed via `GET /admin/mode`), and POSTs `/admin/set-mode` — cheap on idle (gated, fail-closed), fast on command (fire-and-forget, fail-open).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Construction sets `lastOperatorCommandAt = Date.now()` (restart resets to active now; fail-safe fast).
- [ ] An agent-route command records `lastOperatorCommandAt` and fires `POST /admin/set-mode {"mode":"fast"}` fire-and-forget (never blocks or delays dispatch; a failed switch is logged, command proceeds).
- [ ] Cheap switch tick: when `lastOperatorCommandAt` is null/older than `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` AND proxy idle (reuse `evaluateIdle` semantics: llama-server running, no active local query, no model switch, no local lease, all required slots free), POST `{"mode":"cheap"}`. A busy proxy delays the switch (never kills in-flight work).
- [ ] No redundant switching: skip the POST when last-known mode already matches the target; refresh last-known mode via `GET /admin/mode` on poll. At most one switch per state change.
- [ ] `409` (mode-switch restart in progress) is a no-op, retried on a later tick.
- [ ] Fail-closed everywhere: endpoint failures, timeouts, network errors, and ambiguous responses yield no switch and never crash or block the plugin (log a warning).
- [ ] Per-process single-flight: at most one switch in flight at a time.
- [ ] All worker-core tests pass (child WL-0MT1EE3S7005DJ1F).

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` (new)
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` (new)

Depends on settings implementation (WL-0MT1EECPU0024Z7J) and the worker-core test child (WL-0MT1EE3S7005DJ1F, test-first). Reuses `evaluateIdle`/`isIdleStatus`/poller from `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K infra).

## Problem statement

With per-shortcut `open_pane: false` (WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL), commands run detached in the background with output captured to a log file — no pane opens. The selection list currently reflects their effects only on the next auto-refresh cycle: after pressing `a-y` (audit approve) the item stays visible as `in_review` until a refresh happens, so the user gets no deterministic signal that the command finished and the state changed.

## User story

As a worklist user dispatching a background (no-pane) shortcut, I want the selection list to refresh as soon as the command completes, so the updated state (stage/status/priority changes, closed/deleted items) appears without waiting for the periodic refresh.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a background (no-pane) dispatch completes — `spawnBackgroundShell` or `spawnBackgroundPi` child exits — the running TUI instance triggers a refresh of the current view.
2. The completion-triggered refresh is fire-and-forget and non-blocking: it never interferes with the TUI event loop or the dispatched command's own execution; failures are tolerated silently (mirror the existing fire-and-forget patterns in index.ts / worklist.ts).
3. The signal is scoped to the dispatching TUI instance — no global watcher, no cross-instance effects (multiple worklist panes must not refresh each other).
4. Both success (exit 0) and failure (non-zero exit) trigger the refresh; failures remain inspectable via the log path already written to stderr (and may surface a toast with the exit status).
5. Existing behaviour is unchanged: the periodic auto-refresh cycle, and pane-opening dispatch, are untouched.
6. Tests cover the completion → refresh wiring (simulated child exit triggers the refresh callback) and confirm the default (pane-opening) path is unaffected.

## Constraints

- Detached children are unref'd (parent may exit before the child); the completion hook must not require the parent to stay alive beyond dispatch.
- Do not add a global/tmp-file polling watcher if the child 'exit' event suffices (the spawn helpers already return the ChildProcess).
- The refresh entry point lives in the TUI (`runWorklistTui` in packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts); plumb a completion callback (or reuse the existing refresh trigger) rather than duplicating the fetch/merge logic.

## Key files

- packages/herdr/src/index.ts — spawnBackgroundShell / spawnBackgroundPi return ChildProcess; wire `child.on('exit')` to a completion callback.
- packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts — runWorklistTui options gain the completion hook; refresh logic already exists (autoRefresh cycle).
- packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts / worklist.test.ts — tests.

## Related work

- WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL — parent feature that introduced background (no-pane) dispatch; this item makes the results visible deterministically.
- WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9 — work-item ↔ pane association (skipped for no-pane dispatch).
- WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO — list renderer budget/refresh internals.

## Risks & assumptions

- Risk (low): refresh-on-exit could fire while the user is mid-interaction (e.g. typing a search); the existing refresh already handles concurrent user input, so this reuses the same safe path.
- Assumption: the TUI instance that dispatched the command is still alive when the child exits (typical case — panes live for the session); if it exited, the child is unref'd and the callback is a no-op.
data.title: Refresh the selection list when background (no-pane) shortcut commands complete

## Problem statement

The system ground to a halt on 2026-08-20 and required a reboot. RCA identified a cascading failure triggered by an NVIDIA driver API mismatch.

Kernel logs (Aug 20 13:00-13:03) show repeated failures:

```
NVRM: API mismatch: the client chrome-headless (pid 1027619)
```

27,517 such events were logged in one boot (Jul 30 - Aug 8). The kernel module was NVIDIA 595.71.05 while userspace libraries were updated to 595.84. GPU calls silently failed, chrome-headless processes entered retry loops, and memory pressure accumulated until the system became unresponsive.

## Resolution

**Root Cause**: NVIDIA kernel module (595.71.05) vs userspace libraries (595.84) version mismatch.

**Fix**: NVIDIA driver upgraded to 595.84 (Aug 21), system rebooted to kernel 7.0.0-29 with matching kernel module.

## Acceptance Criteria — All Complete

- [x] Identify chrome-headless package and NVIDIA userspace libraries — chrome-headless-shell (Playwright 1.62.1) loads via system libGLX_nvidia.so.0
- [x] Confirm the API mismatch — kernel module 595.71.05 vs userspace 595.84
- [x] Apply a fix — NVIDIA driver upgraded to 595.84, rebooted to kernel 7.0.0-29
- [x] Verify: zero NVRM API mismatch over 24h+ — zero mismatches in current boot (since Aug 20)
- [x] Verify: chrome-headless completes without int3 traps — zero int3 traps in current boot
- [x] Record the fix with exact versions — see audit comment WL-C0MT3N4LCY001IOT6
data.effort: 1–4 hours (estimate: o=1, m=2, p=4) — Small. Diagnostic investigation + targeted fix on a single system. No code changes expected.
data.risk: Medium — NVIDIA driver changes can affect GPU functionality system-wide. Wrong driver version could worsen the problem. Mitigation: test in non-production context first if possible; have rollback plan.
data.title: Fix NVIDIA kernel/userspace driver API mismatch (chrome-headless)

## Problem statement

During the 2026-08-20 system hang, snapd was stuck and required force-kill by systemd:

```
Aug 20 13:37:51 systemd[1]: snapd.service: Watchdog timeout (limit 5min)!
Aug 20 13:37:51 systemd[1]: snapd.service: Killing process 1734095 (snapd) with signal SIGABRT.
Aug 20 13:37:59 systemd[1]: snapd.service: Failed with result 'watchdog'.
Aug 20 13:38:12 systemd[1]: Starting snapd.service - Snap Daemon...
Aug 20 13:39:52 systemd[1]: snapd.service: start operation timed out. Terminating.
```

The snapd SIGABRT stack dump shows the smoking gun: a udev monitor goroutine stuck in an infinite select that never receives events and never times out:

```
goroutine 226 ... [select, 7740 minutes]:
  github.com/snapcore/snapd/overlord/ifacestate/udevmonitor.(*Monitor).Run.func1()
    /build/snapd/.../udevmonitor/udevmon.go:147
```

Multiple goroutines were stuck for hundreds of minutes (IO wait 388 minutes, sync.Cond.Wait 388 minutes). snapd held state locks that other services depended on, contributing to the freeze. The restart also timed out, forcing the reboot.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Confirm whether the snapd udev monitor hang reproduces after a fresh boot (observe over several days; check for stuck goroutines via SIGQUIT dump if it recurs)
- [ ] Research the upstream snapd issue: udevmonitor goroutine never waking from select (snapd bug tracker / launchpad); record the upstream bug reference in a comment
- [ ] Apply mitigation: either update snapd to a fixed version, or if no fix exists, adjust snapd.service WatchdogSec (e.g. disable watchdog via `systemctl set-property snapd.service WatchdogSec=0` or increase it) and document the trade-off
- [ ] Verify snapd stays responsive after mitigation: no watchdog timeouts over a 7-day observation window
- [ ] Record the commit/bug references in comments on this work item

## Key files / commands

- `snap version` (currently snapd 2.76.2 on ubuntu/26.04)
- `journalctl -b -1 -u snapd` for the stack dump evidence
- Discovered from: RCA of system hang 2026-08-20 (session analysis; no parent work item)

- **WL-0MT38GKEP0057T4I** – Document concurrency profile and memory footprint of chrome-headless instances (completed)

# Downtime Dispatch: Spare-Capacity Dispatch (Default N Instead of All-Slots-Free)

## Problem Statement

The herdr downtime worker currently requires ALL llama-proxy slots to be free before dispatching downtime work. With a 3-slot proxy and 1 slot occupied by an active operator session, the worker does nothing — wasting 2 available slots of compute capacity.

## Users

- **Local AI operator** (primary): Wants to work on a task via the TUI while the llama-proxy runs downtime audits/dispatches on spare slots simultaneously.
- **Producer/reviewer**: Benefits from faster audit throughput when spare compute is utilized during operator work sessions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When 2 slots (of 3) have been continuously free for the full idle threshold, downtime dispatch fires — even if 1 slot is occupied by an active (non-processing) session.
2. A mid-query (processing) session on a busy slot does NOT block dispatch into free slots when per-slot identity mode is active.
3. An audit dispatch is only selected when ≥2 slots are free; implement/plan/intake panes require ≥1 free slot.
4. Pre-fix proxies (no per-slot identity) retain the existing all-slots-free fail-closed behaviour; ambiguous payloads are treated as busy.
5. Tests cover: 3 slots/1 busy (dispatch into 2 free), N free of total with a mid-query busy slot, audit 2-slot minimum, old-proxy degradation unchanged.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve fail-closed conventions: ambiguous slot payloads must be treated as busy.
- Per-slot identity detection (proxy serves `slots: [{slot_id, is_processing}]`) must remain opt-in; default behavior for old proxies unchanged.
- CAS claim still serializes concurrent pane dispatches.
- Parallelism accounting: audit phases need `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1` → 2 slots minimum.
- The N > total rule must be preserved (never idle).
- **Default N = 2 of 3 slots** (confirmed decision).

## Existing State

- `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_REQUIRED_FREE_SLOTS = 0` means all slots must be free (`available_slots >= total_slots`).
- `globalIdleChecks` rejects when ANY local query is in flight or a lease is active — blocks spare-capacity regardless of free slots.
- Per-slot identity + same-slot idle tracking already exists (completed WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG, WL-0MSP28LSY007NDYX) but the default and global-busy gate prevent its use for this scenario.

## Desired Change

- Relax the idle gate in per-slot mode: evaluate idle from free slots only, not all slots.
- A query/lease on a busy slot should not block dispatch into 2 free slots (the busy slot that is actively querying is precisely the "active work item" the operator wants to work alongside).
- Set `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_REQUIRED_FREE_SLOTS` to 2 (of 3), so spare-capacity dispatch works out-of-the-box.
- Implement per-slot idle duration tracking in `evaluateIdle` when per-slot data is present and `0 < N < total`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Core idle evaluation and dispatch logic
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (constants) — `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_REQUIRED_FREE_SLOTS`, `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`evaluateIdle`) — Per-slot idle tracking logic
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`globalIdleChecks`) — Global busy checks to relax in per-slot mode
- `packages/herdr/src/herdr-proxy.ts` (or similar) — Proxy slot data parsing
- `packages/herdr/tests/` — Test fixtures and assertions

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG** — Same-slot idle tracking for herdr downtime worker (per slot_id) [COMPLETED]
- **WL-0MSP28LSY007NDYX** — Per-slot identity mechanism [COMPLETED]
- **WL-0MSZ4NSOE007AQEF** — Shortcut key to toggle downtime dispatch per herdr instance [IN PROGRESS]
- **WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8** — Log herdr downtime dispatches [COMPLETED]
- **WL-0MSZS1OHV0067JD1** — Documentation: README update for `d` shortcut and `[Downtime Off]` [COMPLETED]

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- Q: "Does the llama-proxy (192.168.0.199:8000, `GET /slots` broadcast) support concurrent independent requests on different slots?" — Answer: Yes, the router allows a new local dispatch while another session holds a lease / is mid-query. Source: interactive reply (2026-08-21).
- Q: "What should DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_REQUIRED_FREE_SLOTS default to for out-of-the-box spare-capacity dispatch?" — Answer: 2 (of 3 slots), so at least 1 slot is reserved for operator sessions. Source: interactive reply (2026-08-21).
- Q: "Should the setting be a fixed default (e.g. 2 of 3) or a configurable 'reserve N slots for operator' setting?" — Answer: Fixed default of 2 of 3. Source: interactive reply (2026-08-21).
data.title: Downtime dispatch: use available slots while some slots busy (spare-capacity dispatch, default N instead of all-slots-free)

# F3: Per-tier dispatch free-slot minimums

Dispatch-selection slice for WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2: enforce tier-specific minimum free slots at selection time — audit ≥2, implement/plan/intake panes ≥1.

## Goal

An audit dispatch (which needs a second slot for Phase 2 parallelism at `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`) must only be selected when ≥2 slots are free; the pane tiers (implement/plan/intake) need ≥1 free slot. Minimums are evaluated against the latest polled status at selection time, independent of the idle-duration gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Audit tier dispatches only when ≥2 slots are free (parent AC3).
2. Implement/plan/intake tiers dispatch only when ≥1 slot is free (parent AC3).
3. Scheduled-prompt tier follows the pane minimum (≥1 free slot).
4. Minimums evaluated against the latest status at selection time; CAS claim still serializes concurrent pane dispatches (constraints preserved).
5. The idle-duration gate (configured N, default 2) is unchanged — tier minimums are an additional selection-time check.
6. All F1 red tests for tier minimums turn green; full suite passes (parent AC7).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier selection (pass latest free-slot count into tier checks; constants for audit min 2 and pane min 1)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — dispatch-level tier-minimum tests

## Implementation Notes

- Plumb the latest polled free-slot count (or the parsed status) into `dispatchDowntimeWork` so each tier can apply its minimum before the claim.
- Reuse the same fail-closed counting rule: an entry without an explicit boolean `is_processing` is busy, never free.
- Scheduled-prompts and pane tiers share the `PANE_MIN_FREE = 1` constant; audit uses `AUDIT_MIN_FREE = 2`.

# F2: Relax per-slot idle gate + default N=2

Core implementation slice for WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2: in per-slot identity mode, evaluate idle from free slots only so an operator session on a busy slot no longer blocks spare-capacity dispatch; set the out-of-the-box default to 2 of 3 slots.

## Goal

When the proxy serves per-slot identity (`slots: [{slot_id, is_processing}]`) and a configured `0 < N < total`, a query/lease tied to a busy slot must not gate dispatch into the free slots. Old-proxy behavior (no per-slot identity) must stay fail-closed unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Per-slot mode (slots present AND `0 < N < total`): a mid-query (is_processing=true) or leased busy slot does NOT block dispatch into free slots (parent AC2). `llama_server_running` and `model_switch_in_progress` remain global gates; `active_query`/`local_active_query`/`local_lease_active` are superseded by per-slot `is_processing`.
2. `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_REQUIRED_FREE_SLOTS` = 2 (of 3) — spare-capacity dispatch works out-of-the-box (parent AC1).
3. N > total can never be idle; N ≤ 0 keeps the all-slots-free count-based path; ambiguous payloads fail closed to busy (fail-closed conventions preserved).
4. Pre-fix proxies (no per-slot identity): global busy checks unchanged; a configured N with no per-slot data still degrades to all-slots-free (parent AC4).
5. All F1 red tests turn green; full suite passes (parent AC7).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `evaluateIdle` per-slot branch (relax `globalIdleChecks` query/lease in per-slot mode), `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_REQUIRED_FREE_SLOTS` 0 → 2, `createDowntimeWorker.tick()` per-slot routing
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — default setting flows from the changed constant
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — tests turned green

## Implementation Notes

- Introduce a per-slot-safe global check (server up + model switch only) distinct from the full `globalIdleChecks`, used by the per-slot branch of `evaluateIdle` and `tick()`.
- Keep the count-based path (`isIdleStatus`) byte-for-byte unchanged for N ≤ 0 / N ≥ total.
- Default change is a one-line constant edit; verify via tests that the worker's effective default is 2.

# Fix riskOrdinal/effortOrdinal exact-match in packages/shared database.ts (server-side wl next risk/effort filter)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher's implement tier runs `wl next --stage plan_complete --risk medium --effort medium`. The server-side risk/effort filter in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (`riskOrdinal` / `effortOrdinal`, private methods) uses **exact string matching** — identical to the herdr client-side guard that was already fixed (see below).

Items whose risk/effort fields carry verbose agent-produced descriptions are therefore excluded server-side:

- `risk: "Medium — NVIDIA driver changes can affect GPU functionality…"` → `riskOrdinal` returns `null` → filtered out
- `effort: "1–4 hours (estimate: o=1, m=2, p=4) — Small. Diagnostic investigation…"` → `effortOrdinal` returns `null` → filtered out

A genuinely qualified **critical** item (WL-0MT1KJNDK004SNPK, Fix NVIDIA kernel/userspace driver API mismatch) carrying such fields cannot be selected by `wl next --risk medium --effort medium`, silently starving it from implement-tier selection.

## Context / evidence

- `wl show WL-0MT1KJNDK004SNPK --json`: `risk: "Medium — …"` (verbose), `effort: "1–4 hours (estimate: o=1, m=2, p=4) — Small. …"` (verbose)
- `wl next --stage plan_complete --risk medium --effort medium -n 10 --json` does not return WL-0MT1KJNDK004SNPK; `wl next` without the risk/effort filters does not return it either while blocked, but the risk/effort dimension is what excludes it once plan_complete
- The herdr client-side counterpart was fixed in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (downtime-worker.ts `riskOrdinal`/`effortOrdinal`) — the shared server-side copy still has the bug. Discovered-from: WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9 (investigation of dispatcher selection).

## Desired change

Mirror the herdr fix in `packages/shared/src/database.ts`:

1. `riskOrdinal` — extract the leading keyword before any delimiter (`-`, `:`, `–`, `—`, whitespace), then match (low/medium/high/severe/critical). Verbose "Medium — …" must map to 2.
2. `effortOrdinal` — keep the stripped-string exact match for simple cases ("Extra Small" → "extrasmall"), then fall back to a word-boundary search for the keyword anywhere in the string ("1–4 hours — Small…" → finds small). Short spellings (XS/S/M/L/XL) and long forms must keep working.
3. Fallback safety: items with unparseable/unset risk or effort remain **excluded** (fail-closed unchanged); only the verbose-description form becomes recognized.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `wl next --stage plan_complete --risk medium --effort medium` returns an item whose risk is `"Medium — <verbose description>"` and effort is `"… — Small. <verbose description>"` (reproduce with WL-0MT1KJNDK004SNPK's exact field values once it is at plan_complete and unblocked)
- [ ] Unit tests cover verbose risk and verbose effort server-side matching, plus regression that high/severe risk is still excluded by an at-most medium filter
- [ ] Short spellings (xs/s/m/l/xl) and long forms (extra small / extra large) continue to work as before
- [ ] Full project test suite passes

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `riskOrdinal` / `effortOrdinal` (private methods around lines 1555–1620) + `matchesRiskEffort`
- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` (or the equivalent suite) — new tests

## Related work

- **WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9** — dispatch whose investigation uncovered the bug (discovered-from)
- **WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6** — implement tier (the tier whose `wl next` invocation is affected)

# Downtime dispatcher: critical items always progress first, regardless of stage

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher's tiers select candidates at a **fixed stage**: implement tier requires `plan_complete`, plan tier requires `intake_complete`, intake tier requires `idea`. A **critical** item that is still at `idea` or `intake_complete` waits in the backlog while non-critical items at `plan_complete` are dispatched first — even though the critical item could be progressed immediately with the stage-appropriate skill (`/skill:intake`, `/skill:plan`, `/skill:implement`).

Concrete case (2026-08-21): WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9 (medium, plan_complete) was dispatched for implement ahead of critical items WL-0MT1KJNDK004SNPK / WL-0MT1KJNHY00286QE, which were still at `idea`. The dispatcher's stage-first selection treats a ready medium item as higher priority than a critical item that merely hasn't been progressed yet.

## Users

- **Operator** — wants critical items (system stability, security, broken builds) worked immediately, with the stage-appropriate skill, not gated behind the fixed tier order.
- **Downtime dispatcher consumers** — wants the dispatch queue to reflect true priority regardless of workflow stage.
- Example user story: "As an operator, when a critical item is still at `idea`, I want the downtime worker to run `/skill:intake` on it before any non-critical implement dispatch."

## Desired change

Add a **critical-first pre-tier** to the dispatch loop (`dispatchDowntimeWork`):

1. On each dispatch tick (after the audit tier — audits are complete-work verification and keep their slot; before the non-critical implement/plan/intake tiers), scan for any **open** item with `priority = critical`.
2. If found, dispatch the skill that advances its current stage:
   - `idea` → `/skill:intake <id>`
   - `intake_complete` → `/skill:plan <id>`
   - `plan_complete` → `/skill:implement <id>` (subject to risk/effort caps — decision Q2 below)
   - Any other stage (e.g. `in_progress`, `in_review`) → not a dispatch target (already being worked or awaiting review).
3. If multiple critical items, select deterministically: earliest `sortIndex` (wl priority order) with the existing round-robin tie-break within the critical group.
4. The critical-first tier **replaces** the stage-gated tiers for critical items — a critical item at any stage wins over every non-critical candidate at any stage. Non-critical items fall back to the existing tier order (implement → plan → intake) unchanged.

## Decisions (operator-confirmed 2026-08-21)

- **Q1 — Code-freeze gate (decision: split by skill).** During a ship-it freeze (marker `frozen` or `ambiguous`, fail-closed), **critical implement dispatch pauses** — same fresh-read freeze gate as the existing implement tier (WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY), so no new code lands mid-release. **Critical plan/intake dispatch continues** during a freeze, consistent with the existing plan/intake tiers which already run while frozen (no new code). When the freeze lifts, critical implement dispatch resumes.
- **Q2 — Risk/effort caps (decision: keep the caps).** Critical implement dispatch retains the implement tier's risk ≤ Medium / effort ≤ Medium caps (client-side ordinal filter in `selectImplementCandidate`). A critical item at `plan_complete` with High risk or Large effort is **not** implement-dispatched by the downtime worker — it waits for explicit (human/session) handling. Accepted limitation; the ticket's consumer is the dispatch queue, not a guarantee that every critical item can be dispatched.
- **Q3 — Dependency-blocked critical items (decision: dependency frontier).** When the selected critical candidate is dependency-blocked, follow the blocking chain and dispatch the **nearest open blocker** with its own stage-appropriate skill (the dependency frontier): `idea` → `/skill:intake`, `intake_complete` → `/skill:plan`, `plan_complete` → `/skill:implement` (caps apply to implement). Recurse while blockers are themselves dependency-blocked. A frontier item at a non-dispatchable stage (e.g. `in_progress`, `in_review`) or a chain that bottoms out in closed items → no dispatch from the critical tier, fall through to the normal tier order.

## Constraints (composition with existing guards)

- **Claim/CAS, dispatched-marker change-guard, single-flight**: the critical-first tier must compose with the existing pre-dispatch claim (CAS `if-stage` guard) and the dispatched-marker exclusion (`dispatchedStages` map: an item is excluded while still at its dispatched-at stage; stage advancement releases it). A critical item must not be double-dispatched, and a dispatched run reverting to the same stage must not re-select. Per-process single-flight (`dispatchInFlight`) applies unchanged.
- **One dispatch per idle tick**: the critical-first tier dispatches at most ONE item per tick (single-dispatch semantics preserved).
- **Tier ordering**: scheduled-prompts tier first (unchanged), then audit tier (its slot is kept — completed-work verification does not wait behind new critical work), then critical-first tier, then non-critical implement → plan → intake.
- **Dispatched-marker `kind` mapping**: critical-first dispatch keeps the same kind mapping to the skill used (`implement`/`plan`/`intake`), so the rolling log and change-guard stay consistent.
- **Stage skip on dispatch log / kind**: unchanged from existing tiers.

## Existing state

`dispatchDowntimeWork` (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:1137) runs, in order: scheduled-prompts (WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX), audit (completed/in_review, 7-day recency, root-only), implement (`plan_complete`, risk/effort-capped, dispatched-marker change-guard, round-robin), plan (`intake_complete`), intake (`idea`). A fresh-read code-freeze marker gates scheduled-prompts/audit/implement; plan/intake tiers run during freezes. Candidate selection helpers: `selectImplementCandidate` (risk/effort ordinal caps), `selectNextCandidate` (stage-change-guard), `selectWithRotation` (round-robin). `wl next --stage <stage>` excludes dependency-blocked items by default — the critical lookup cannot rely on it alone (Q3 needs explicit dep resolution).

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier ordering + new critical-first selection (`selectCriticalCandidate`), dependency-frontier resolution (`resolveDependencyFrontier` or equivalent), `DowntimeWorkerDeps` additions
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — test-first matrix: per-stage progression, priority ordering, freeze interplay, dependency-blocked interplay, caps, no double-dispatch
- Possibly `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — a stage-agnostic critical lookup query (critical items including dependency-blocked ones, with dep/blocker edges for the frontier) reusing the sortIndex/priority ordering

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An open critical item at `idea` is dispatched with `/skill:intake` ahead of any non-critical `plan_complete` item
- [ ] An open critical item at `intake_complete` is dispatched with `/skill:plan` ahead of any non-critical `plan_complete` item
- [ ] An open critical item at `plan_complete` with risk ≤ Medium / effort ≤ Medium is dispatched with `/skill:implement` ahead of any non-critical item at any stage (caps retained — decision Q2)
- [ ] A critical `plan_complete` item above the risk/effort caps is NOT dispatched by the critical tier (caps retained)
- [ ] Multiple critical items select deterministically (sortIndex + round-robin tie-break), never double-dispatched (claim CAS + dispatched-marker guards hold)
- [ ] During a code freeze: critical implement dispatch pauses (fail-closed on ambiguous marker), critical plan/intake dispatch continues (decision Q1)
- [ ] A dependency-blocked critical item dispatches its nearest open blocker (dependency frontier) with the blocker's stage-appropriate skill; chains bottoming out in closed/non-dispatchable items fall through to the normal tiers (decision Q3)
- [ ] Non-critical items keep the existing tier order when no critical item exists (no behavior change)
- [ ] Unit tests cover: critical-first progression per stage, priority ordering, freeze interplay, dependency-blocked interplay, caps retention, no double-dispatch
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9** — the dispatch whose selection motivated this item (medium item dispatched ahead of critical items at earlier stages)
- **WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6** — implement tier (fixed-stage selection this item supersedes for critical items; caps reused per decision Q2)
- **WL-0MT1KJNDK004SNPK / WL-0MT1KJNHY00286QE** — the critical items that waited while a medium item was dispatched
- **WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6** — round-robin selection (tie-break to reuse)
- **WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY** — code-freeze gate (interplay resolved by decision Q1)
- **WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX** — scheduled-prompts tier (ordering constraint: stays first)
- **WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B** — server-side risk/effort exact-match fix (a critical item's verbose risk/effort fields blocked selection; prerequisite for reliable capped critical implement probing)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** changing tier ordering can starve non-critical work if critical items are continuously created — mitigated by dispatching only ONE item per idle period (existing single-dispatch) and by re-sort semantics.
- **Risk:** critical items at `plan_complete` above the risk/effort caps will not be dispatched by downtime (decision Q2) — mitigated by documenting this as an accepted limitation; the caps keep High-risk items out of autonomous implementation.
- **Risk:** dependency-frontier dispatch (Q3) may dispatch a non-critical blocker onto the critical path — accepted: it is the only way to progress the critical item autonomously; the blocker's own stage-appropriate skill still applies.
- **Scope-creep guard:** out of scope for this item — critical-first dispatch for high/medium/low priorities, critical-bypass of the freeze, cap relaxation, and multi-item dispatch per tick. Extra opportunities found during implementation are recorded as linked work items, not added to this item.
- **Assumption:** audit tier keeps its slot ahead of critical-first (verifying completed work does not wait behind new critical work) — confirmed during planning.
- **Assumption:** `wl` provides (or can be queried for) dependency edges for open items without excluding blocked critical items (needed for the critical lookup + frontier).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "During a ship-it freeze, should critical-first dispatch honor the freeze (pause all), bypass it entirely (critical items dispatch even mid-freeze), or split by skill (intake/plan run — no new code — while implement pauses)?" — Answer (operator): "c. Split by skill: critical intake/plan still run (no new code), critical implement pauses with the freeze." Source: interactive intake reply 2026-08-21. Research: freeze gate WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY skips audit/implement tiers while plan/intake tiers keep running; split-by-skill is consistent with that existing posture.
- Q2: "Should critical-first implement dispatch ignore the risk/effort caps (a High-risk critical item can be implement-dispatched) or keep them?" — Answer (operator): "b. Keep the caps — so a High-risk critical item isn't implement-dispatched." Source: interactive intake reply 2026-08-21. Note: this reverses the recommendation originally drafted in the description ("recommend: ignore caps"); the brief now reflects the operator decision. Research: caps live in `selectImplementCandidate` (risk ≤ Medium / effort ≤ Medium ordinal filters); WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B fixes verbose-field blocking.
- Q3: "When the selected critical item is dependency-blocked, should dispatch target the blocking item instead (dependency frontier, recursion into blockers), fall through to the normal tier order, or skip blocked critical items entirely?" — Answer (operator): "a. Dispatch the blocking item instead if it's open (dependency frontier — recursion into blockers)." Source: interactive intake reply 2026-08-21. Research: `wl next --stage` excludes dependency-blocked items, so the critical lookup must resolve dep edges explicitly; `wl dep list <id>` provides the edges.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT** – RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (audit + possibly other work) (completed)
- **WL-0MSJ4BT4Z002HH9B** – Fully remove deprecated icons.ts from all projects that use it (src + herdr) (open)
- **WL-0MSZ4NSOE007AQEF** – Shortcut key to toggle downtime dispatch per herdr instance (in-progress)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — dispatch tiers/guards documentation (implement/audit tier, freeze gate, round-robin)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MT1KLQYD004MOQT-flaky-worklog-dir-delegation-test/packages/herdr/README.md` — worktree copy of the same README

# Intake Brief: Dispatching continues while downtime dispatch is disabled

**Work item:** WL-0MT4BWUHW008LIFE · **Type:** bug · **Priority:** critical (operator-specified)
**Date:** 2026-08-22

## Problem statement

The operator disables downtime dispatch via the `d` shortcut (header shows
`[Downtime Off]` on the pane) yet pi agent work continues to be dispatched —
audits, plans and implementations keep spawning, and the ContextHub audit
`WL-0MSKSMRFP001Q3XU` was dispatched at 11:05:23Z while the operator believed
dispatch was disabled. The same herdr worklist header later reported
`[⏳ downtime idle 40+ min]` — the enabled-and-idle worker state — in a
session the operator considers disabled. The disable control is not
effective, not durable, or not scoped the way the operator believes.

## Users

- **Herdr operators (multi-workspace)**: disable downtime dispatch to stop
  autonomous work (e.g. while working interactively), and expect that disable
  to hold — without needing to also stop every sibling pane or remember
  in-memory semantics.
  - As an operator I press `d`, see `[Downtime Off]`, and **no** new pi agent
    panes spawn anywhere for that worklog root until I re-enable dispatch.
  - As an operator I can tell, at a glance, which pane(s) are disabled and
    which are still dispatching.

## Acceptance Criteria (initial; refine at plan)

1. **Disabled ⇒ no dispatch, durably.** After one `d` press (header shows
   `[Downtime Off]`), with no further key presses and no manual settings edit,
   the worklist's downtime worker performs no proxy polling, no idle
   tracking, and no dispatch **for at least 60 minutes** (i.e. well past the
   4-minute idle threshold and any 60-minute no-candidate cooldown window).
   Verified by a test that toggles the worker off, advances simulated time
   through the threshold/cooldown boundaries, and asserts zero
   `dispatchDowntimeWork` invocations and zero pane spawns.
2. **No silent re-enable.** If the per-instance override can be lost by any
   real pane/plugin lifecycle event (restart, reload, re-attach), the
   operator must be told explicitly (header/status must not silently return
   to `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]` in a pane previously shown `[Downtime Off]`).
   The chosen fix must make the disable state either (a) durable across those
   events, or (b) visibly non-durable with an explicit notice — never a
   silent revert.
3. **Toggle cycle cannot force-enable.** Pressing `d` twice must never leave
   dispatch force-enabled (`override === true`) while the operator believes
   they disabled it: the second press returns to "follow settings" (`null`),
   or re-enable requires explicit confirmation. A test pins the full cycle
   `null → false → null` (or `null → false → (confirmed) true` — decided at
   plan) and asserts `enabled` after each step.
4. **Header honesty.** `renderDowntimeStatus` must never render
   `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]` (an enabled, polling worker) in a pane whose
   dispatch gate the operator disabled: the rendered state must always agree
   with the effective dispatch decision of `tick()`. Test: render off /
   enabled / paused / dispatching states against the worker's effective
   enabled state.
5. **Per-pane scope is visible & documented.** The per-instance scope of the
   `d` toggle is preserved (sibling panes unaffected), but the README/help
   makes the scope explicit ("current pane only, in-memory, resets on
   restart"), and each pane's header state (`[Downtime Off]` vs live status)
   lets the operator tell which pane is disabled. Docs updated; acceptance: a
   user reading the README cannot reasonably believe `d` disables dispatch
   for all panes or persists across restarts.
6. **Root-cause regression evidence.** The reproducing evidence for the
   reported incident — ContextHub audit `WL-0MSKSMRFP001Q3XU` dispatched
   2026-08-22T11:05:23Z while dispatch was believed disabled, and the
   subsequent 11:05–11:47Z multi-root dispatch wave — is explained by the
   confirmed root cause in a comment/AC write-up, with the confirmation
   steps used (dispatch-log, herdr pane-spawn log, header state).
7. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (including the
   existing downtime-worker / toggle test suites
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts`).

## Constraints

- The per-instance in-memory toggle design (WL-0MSZ4NSOE007AQEF AC2) may be
  changed ONLY where needed to satisfy AC2/AC3; settings file writes and
  cross-pane coupling need explicit operator sign-off at plan.
- Existing dispatch guarantees must not regress: code-freeze gate, dispatched
  marker exclusion, per-tier free-slot minimums, single-flight, no-candidate
  cooldown (see RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT and
  `packages/herdr/docs/downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`).
- No new dispatch side channels: the fix must not add or remove a dispatch
  mechanism; it only changes when the existing worker dispatches.

## Existing state

- The `d` shortcut (shortcuts.json) → `/downtime toggle` →
  `onDowntimeToggle()` → `downtimeWorker.toggle()` (index.ts:1000-1046,
  worklist.ts:3346-3352).
- `toggle()` cycles the in-memory override `null → false → true → null`
  (downtime-worker.ts:1639-1641): **a second press force-enables dispatch
  (override = true)**, which also overrides a settings-level disable.
- `tick()` short-circuits when `!(override ?? cfg.enabled)`
  (downtime-worker.ts:1658-1661) — the gate is correct for a single worker
  instance.
- `renderDowntimeStatus` (worklist.ts:2771-2799) renders either
  `[Downtime Off]` (disabled) or `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]`
  (enabled + polling): mutually exclusive for one pane.
- The toggle is **in-memory and per-instance**: plugin/pane restart resets
  `override` to `null` (follows settings) with no notice; sibling panes are
  unaffected. Leader-only dispatch (WL-0MSXHA1B0005G3E5) is blocked, so
  multiple panes dispatch concurrently.
- Observed evidence 2026-08-22 (report incident):
  - ContextHub `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`: audit
    `WL-0MSKSMRFP001Q3XU` dispatched 11:05:23Z (cwd ContextHub); last entry
    for this root.
  - herdr-server.log: four dispatch panes spawned simultaneously 11:05:09–
    11:05:23Z across SorraAgents / open_source_llm / Tableau-Card-Engine /
    ContextHub (pids 302077/302156/302252/302464); further panes 11:12Z,
    11:15Z, 11:42Z, 11:47Z (sibling roots only).
  - No worklist-pane (plugin) restart is evident in herdr-server.log between
    the incident and the report; the `/downtime toggle` press itself is not
    recorded in worklog-command-log.json (internal action, unlogged).
  - Config `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` has no `downtimeEnabled`
    key → all workers enabled by default.

## Desired change

Downtime dispatch, once disabled, must actually stop dispatching for the
worklog root the operator is controlling and stay stopped until explicitly
re-enabled — with the header state always agreeing with the effective gate,
and with the per-pane/in-memory scope either made durable or made explicit.
Root-cause confirmation at implementation must decide between (ranked):

- **H1 — override lost/cycled after the press:** pane/plugin lifecycle or a
  second `d` press reverted the override (`null` → settings-enabled, or
  `false` → `true` force-on). Explains the audit dispatch at 11:05:23Z and
  the later idle-40+min header. Validation: reproduce toggle → restart /
  second press → assert dispatch resumes silently (AC2/AC3).
- **H2 — in-flight dispatch completed after the press:** a dispatch already
  running when `d` was pressed completed (single-flight; marker written after
  spawn). Explains one late dispatch, not the continued idle reporting.
  Validation: press `d` while `dispatching === true`; assert the in-flight
  dispatch still logs (acceptable) but no NEW dispatch starts (AC1).
- **H3 — scope mismatch:** the observed dispatch came from another enabled
  pane (sibling workspace/root) while the toggled pane was correctly off.
  Explains continuing sibling-root dispatches and an idle header in an
  untoggled pane. Validation: enumerate panes/workspaces, reproduce
  per-instance toggle (AC5).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `toggle()` cycle (~1639),
  `tick()` gate (~1658), `createDowntimeWorker` override lifecycle; where
  durable-override and cycle fixes land.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `renderDowntimeStatus` (~2771),
  `/downtime toggle` routing (3346), scheduler task registration (5066);
  header-honesty fix, persisted-state notice, README-adjacent help hints.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — worker wiring + `onDowntimeToggle`
  (~1000-1046); sole `createDowntimeWorker` call site.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `PluginSettings` schema (43-79);
  durable override key if persistence is chosen (constraint: needs sign-off).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `d` → `/downtime toggle` (line 4).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — scope/durability documentation (AC5).
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`.
- Evidence: `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`,
  `~/.config/herdr/herdr-server.log`,
  `~/.config/herdr/worklog-command-log.json`.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSZ4NSOE007AQEF** — Shortcut key to toggle downtime dispatch per
  herdr instance (parent design; in_review). AC2 mandates in-memory
  per-instance; AC4 mandates the tick short-circuit. This bug is the first
  real-world failure of that design's durability/scope expectations.
- **WL-0MSZS1NNV0075NFI** — Header rendering `[Downtime Off]` (completed).
- **WL-0MSZS1OHV0067JD1** — README docs for `d` / `[Downtime Off]`
  (completed; docs now need the scope/durability caveat).
- **WL-0MSXHA1B0005G3E5** — Leader-only dispatch logic (blocked): while
  unimplemented, multiple panes dispatch concurrently, amplifying any
  per-pane disable gap.
- **WL-0MT47BMR7003ZQ66** — Active-audit single-flight tests (open): audit
  dispatch multiplicity guard, adjacent to the reported multi-dispatch wave.
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY / WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT** — Prior downtime dispatch
  duplication RCA + fix (completed): dispatch-path guarantees this fix must
  not regress.
- Docs: `packages/herdr/docs/downtime-config-audit-2026-08-08.md`,
  `packages/herdr/docs/downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — single root cause may not exist:** the evidence is
  consistent with H1+H3 jointly (override lost AND sibling panes dispatching
  regardless). ACs are written against the observable contract so the fix
  covers the failure class, not one mechanism.
- **Risk — persistence changes settings semantics:** making the override
  durable (e.g. writing a per-project marker) touches the shared settings /
  marker files and could affect multi-pane behavior; needs operator sign-off
  at plan (constraint).
- **Risk — scope creep:** attractive extras (global kill switch, per-project
  master disable, leader-only completion) are adjacent but out of scope;
  file as follow-ups, do not fold in.
- **Mitigation — evidence kit preserved:** dispatch log, herdr pane-spawn
  log excerpts and header-state observations are recorded above and in work
  item comments so the implementer can verify the confirmed root cause
  without guessing.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How did you disable dispatching? (a) pressed `d` → header showed
  `[Downtime Off]` on the pane you were looking at; (b) set `downtimeEnabled:
  false` in the herdr config; (c) something else?" — Answer (operator,
  interactive): **(a)** pressed `d`, header showed `[Downtime Off]`.
- Q2: "Where does the 'idle 40+ minutes' report appear?" — Answer
  (operator, interactive): **the herdr worklist header
  (`[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]`)**.
- Q3: "Which audit dispatch violated your disable intent?" — Answer
  (operator, interactive): **`WL-0MSKSMRFP001Q3XU`** (ContextHub root;
  dispatched 2026-08-22T11:05:23Z per dispatch log; pane spawned
  11:05:23.495Z per herdr-server.log).
- OPEN QUESTION 1: Was `d` pressed exactly once in the flagged pane, or more
  than once? (Discriminates H1-cycle from H1-restart / H3.)
- OPEN QUESTION 2: Which workspace/tab displayed `[Downtime Off]` vs the
  header showing `[⏳ downtime idle 40+ min]` — the same pane or different
  panes? (Discriminates H3.)
- OPEN QUESTION 3: Was the flagged worklist pane restarted/re-attached
  between the `d` press and the observed dispatch? (herdr-server.log shows no
  plugin-pane respawn in the window, but herdr may not log all lifecycle
  events.)
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MT3IA1UB005TLVJ** – Tier wiring: freeze split-by-skill & guard composition (completed)
- **WL-0MM0BM7B10QXA3KN** – Tests and CI coverage for ID search cases (completed)
- **WL-0MSKH1J0R003BM2M** – Add issue-type gating to herdr shortcuts; limit code-focused shortcuts to code work item types (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: audit, bug, continues, currently, disabled (+15 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: audit, bug, continues, disabled, extension (+9 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: audit, bug, dispatch, dispatched, downtime (+8 more)



## Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-23: Plan created via /skill:plan. 8 children created (3 test-first, 3 implementation, 1 docs, 1 root-cause write-up); all promoted to priority critical (operator direction). All 7 parent ACs mapped to child coverage.
- Automated review stages: (1) Requirements & AC alignment — added 60-minute no-dispatch AC to marker test (parent AC1 coverage); (2) Completeness — repaired corrupted T1 description (backtick shell mangling) and R1 Key Files format; (3) Sequencing — added R1→I3 dependency (write-up after header notice); (4) Scope sizing — no change; (5) Testability — no change; (6) Polish — Appendix appended below.
- Parent AC coverage verified via tree-coverage helper (recommendation: proceed). Note: `wl show --children` returns empty due to a tooling quirk; parent linkage verified per-child via parentId and `wl list --parent`.

## Appendix: plan-session clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Proposed plan requires confirmation because its risk is High — accept, edit, reorder, or split?" Answer (operator): **LGTM, make this a critical item**. Final: plan accepted as proposed; all 8 children set to priority critical.
- OPEN QUESTION (inherited from intake, unresolved): Was `d` pressed exactly once or more than once in the flagged pane? — to be answered by the root-cause confirmation write-up (WL-0MT5SMVXS004T3BK) from logs where possible.

# F3-fix: implement tier missing panesEligible free-slot guard

Bug found by re-audit of WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 (2026-08-22, F3 AC2 partial): the implement tier in dispatchDowntimeWork has a 'Pane minimum' comment (downtime-worker.ts:1336) but NO panesEligible guard (downtime-worker.ts:1328-1341) — a direct dispatchDowntimeWork({freeSlots:0}) still dispatches implement. Only unreachable via the worker because the idle gate (N>=1, default 2) guarantees ≥1 free slot first.

## Goal

Make the implement tier honor the ≥1 free-slot pane minimum at selection time, matching the critical/audit/plan/intake tiers — so a direct dispatchDowntimeWork({freeSlots:0}) never dispatches implement.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The implement tier dispatches only when ≥1 free slot is available at selection time (dispatchDowntimeWork({freeSlots:0}) never dispatches implement).
2. With freeSlots >= 1 the implement tier behaves exactly as before (no regression to normal worker dispatch).
3. With freeSlots undefined (direct legacy callers) the implement tier is not gated (fail-open preserved, matching all other tiers).
4. The 0-free-slot defensive path returns no-candidate (matching the plan tier's defensive path) rather than dispatching.
5. Ensure F1/F2/F3 existing tests still pass; add regression test(s) cover AC1/AC3/AC4.
6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

# F3 — Surface FTS5 syntax errors: auto-quote with warning

## Target outcome

Stop silently swallowing FTS5 query syntax errors. Unquoted punctuated terms (versions, paths, ids — e.g. `v0.1.11`) are auto-quoted as a phrase and searched, with a **visible warning** in the output; when auto-quoting also fails, the error is surfaced with a non-zero exit (parent AC2, producer decision Q2=B).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl search v0.1.11` (unquoted punctuated term) returns matches AND prints a visible warning that the term was interpreted as a phrase — never a silent empty result.
2. A query that fails even when auto-quoted exits non-zero with a clear `invalid query — quote phrases`-style message (parent AC2 fallback).
3. Genuinely zero-match queries still print "No results found." and exit 0.
4. JSON mode reports the change via structured fields (`success`, `error`, `warning`) without contaminating `workItems`.
5. Non-syntax DB errors are no longer masked as empty results (logged with context; distinguished from `no matches`).

## Minimal Implementation

- `searchFts` (packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts ~line 1623): classify the catch — FTS5 syntax errors (message matches `fts5: syntax error near …`) trigger an auto-quote retry (raw query wrapped as a quoted phrase); if the retry succeeds, return results with an "auto-quoted" signal; if it fails, throw a typed error. Other DB errors are rethrown with context.
- `Db.search()` (packages/shared/src/database.ts ~line 778): propagate results + optional warning/error surrogates without breaking the existing `{ results, ftsUsed }` shape (extend, don't remove fields).
- `src/commands/search.ts`: print the warning on auto-quote; on unhandleable syntax error call `output.error(...)` + `process.exit(1)`; include warning/error in the JSON payload.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing search result shape for downstream consumers (`FtsSearchResult[]`); additive changes only.
- Keep the fallback path (`searchFallback`) untouched.

## Dependencies

- F1 (error-surface tests exist first; red before this work, green after).

## Deliverables

- Code changes; compiled dist refreshed; F1 error tests green; `wl search v0.1.11` behavior verified in CLI integration.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts`

# Repeat Questions in Final Summary When Dispatched in Downtime

## Problem

When the herdr downtime worker dispatches work items to agents, the dispatched prompt instructs agents to record questions in a comment when they cannot proceed — but does **not** tell them to repeat those questions in their final summary. As a result, the producer may not see the questions directly in the agent's report and must dig into the work-item comment to find them.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The `BLOCKED_QUESTIONS_INSTRUCTION` constant in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` includes an instruction to repeat questions in the final summary.**
   - The instruction appears verbatim in the built prompt sent to the agent pane.
   - Example phrasing: *"repeat the questions in your final summary"* or equivalent clear directive.

2. **The existing `buildDowntimePrompt` function still produces valid prompts.**
   - The prompt still contains the original blocked-questions instructions (record questions, flag needs-producer-review, stop).
   - All existing test assertions in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` continue to pass.

3. **Test coverage: new test verifies the final-summary instruction is present.**
   - A new test case checks that `BLOCKED_QUESTIONS_INSTRUCTION` contains the final-summary directive.
   - A new test case checks that `buildDowntimePrompt` output contains the directive.

4. **README documentation is updated to reflect the new instruction.**
   - The "Blocked-questions handling" section in `packages/herdr/README.md` mentions the final-summary instruction.

## Constraints

- Change is minimal: a single string constant + tests + doc update.
- Must not break any existing behavior — only ADD an instruction.
- The `dist/` files are gitignored build output (not committed).

## Existing State

The prompt is built in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`:

```
BLOCKED_QUESTIONS_INSTRUCTION =
  'If you cannot proceed because you need answers, record the questions in a ' +
  'comment on the work item (wl comment add <id> --comment "question: ...") and ' +
  'mark the item as needing producer review (wl update <id> --needs-producer-review ' +
  'true), then stop — do not block indefinitely.';
```

## Desired Change

Append an instruction to the `BLOCKED_QUESTIONS_INSTRUCTION` string that tells the agent to repeat the questions in its final summary.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — update `BLOCKED_QUESTIONS_INSTRUCTION`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — add test for the new instruction
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — update documentation

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** — Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime (parent downtime dispatch)
- **WL-0MSKUFZXV005HWUY** — Verify wedge fix deployment (related: agent panes in downtime)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **toggle() cycles null → false → null.** After two toggle() calls from null, override is null (not true).
2. **Single disable works.** After one toggle() from null, override is false and enabled is false.
3. **tick() short-circuits when disabled.** After toggle() sets override to false, tick() returns {polled:false, dispatched:false, idle:false}.
4. **No force-enable on second press.** The cycle must NOT go through true — the second press returns to null (follow settings), never force-enables dispatch.
5. **All existing tests pass.** The pre-existing toggle cycle test and related tests update to reflect the new null→false→null cycle.

## Goal

Every wl spawn in the herdr refresh/sync fetch path gets a bounded default timeout so a hung `wl` (e.g. blocked on the worklog lock during a long `wl sync`, or a stuck child) can never wedge the `refreshInFlight` single-flight guard (worklist.ts) permanently.

## Background

`runWlInner` (packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:339) forwards `timeout` to `execFileAsync` only when `timeoutMs !== undefined`; no refresh-path caller (`fetchNextItems`, `fetchItemsByStage`, `fetchItemsByPriority`, `fetchMandatorySubsets`, `fetchActionableCount`, `fetchChildrenForItem`, `runWlSync`) supplies one. `doRefresh` (worklist.ts:3984) awaits these inside the `refreshInFlight` guard; a hang means the `finally` never runs and every subsequent refresh is skipped forever. `auto-sync.ts`'s `runSync` already has a 60s spawn safety timeout; `claimItem` already passes `CLAIM_TIMEOUT_MS=3000`. This item adopts the same convention for the read/fetch path.

## Suggested approach (approved)

Add `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` in fetcher.ts and apply it inside `runWl`/`runWlInner` when the caller omits `timeoutMs` (e.g. `timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS`), keeping per-call overrides intact. Verify no existing tests depend on unbounded spawns (they run through the injectable exec seam and resolve immediately, so they should be unaffected).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS` (60_000) is exported from fetcher.ts and documented as the default bound for wl spawns.
- [ ] `runWl`/`runWlInner` apply the default when the caller omits `timeoutMs`; an explicit caller-provided `timeoutMs` still wins (e.g. `CLAIM_TIMEOUT_MS=3000` unchanged).
- [ ] All refresh/sync fetch-path spawns are bounded via the default (fetchNextItems, fetchItemsByStage, fetchItemsByPriority, fetchMandatorySubsets, fetchActionableCount, fetchChildrenForItem, runWlSync).
- [ ] A timed-out refresh fails gracefully: the fetch rejects, `doRefresh` shows the `Refresh failed` toast and clears the guard in `finally`, and the next auto-refresh tick retries — never a permanently wedged `refreshInFlight`.
- [ ] All packages/herdr unit tests pass.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts
- packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts

# Problem

In per-slot mode (spare-capacity dispatch), the herdr title bar displays `[⏳ downtime idle Xs]` even when the llama UI shows the model is actively processing a query. This is because the global idle tracker used for the title bar display uses `perSlotGlobalIdleChecks()` which deliberately ignores `local_active_query` and `local_lease_active`.

# Root Cause

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `createDowntimeWorker.tick()` (line ~2547):

```javascript
const globalIdle = perSlotGlobalIdleChecks(status);
tracker.record(globalIdle);
```

`perSlotGlobalIdleChecks` (line ~295) only checks `llama_server_running` and `!model_switch_in_progress`. It deliberately ignores query activity because the operator's busy slot is their own session and should NOT block downtime dispatch. However, this same relaxed check drives the **display** via `tracker.idleSince` — the title bar idle indicator reflects this relaxed gate, not actual query activity.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **When the llama UI shows active query processing**, the herdr title bar MUST show `[downtime busy]` (not `[⏳ downtime idle Xs]`)
2. **When no query is active** AND sufficient free slots exist for the configured threshold duration, the title bar MUST show `[⏳ downtime idle Xs]` with the elapsed counter
3. **In per-slot mode**, the display MUST reflect per-slot `is_processing` status — if ANY slot is processing (including the operator's slot), the title bar shows busy
4. **Existing behavior is preserved** — the dispatch logic (spare-capacity relaxation: operator's busy slot does NOT block dispatch into free slots) is unchanged; only the **display** is corrected
5. **All existing unit tests pass** — especially `downt-worker.test.ts` idle tracking tests and `worklist.test.ts` `renderDowntimeStatus` tests

# Proposed Fix

Two approaches (least invasive preferred):

**Approach A (display-only):** In `renderDowntimeStatus`, pass an additional `status` or `localActiveQuery` flag to override the idle display. This keeps the global tracker's relaxed semantics for dispatch decisions while fixing the display.

**Approach B (tracker-level):** Add a `globalActiveQuery` field to `IdleTracker` — in per-slot mode, call `tracker.record(false)` when `local_active_query` is true, regardless of the relaxed per-slot checks. This aligns the tracker with actual busy state.

Approach A is preferred (display-only change, minimal risk).

# Affected Files
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `createDowntimeWorker` tick loop, idle tracker
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `renderDowntimeStatus` (line ~2778)

# Constraints
- Dispatch logic must remain unchanged: spare-capacity relaxation (operator's busy slot does not block downtime into free slots) is intentional and must be preserved
- The fix is display-only: correcting the idle indicator in the title bar
- Backward compatible with pre-per-slot-mode proxies (no per-slot data)

# Related Work

- WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K — Header rendering: `[Downtime Off]` status text (parent)
- WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 — Spare-capacity dispatch (parent of per-slot relaxation)

# Fix prefix-to-sibling scan for non-framework repos

## Problem

When the audit skill runs from a non-framework repo (like ContextHub with WL prefix), the prefix-to-sibling scan fails to find the worklog directory because `SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT` points to the wrong level.

### Root cause

`_resolve_repo_root()` in `shared/status_lifecycle.py` finds the directory containing `skill/shared/` (e.g. `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`), but doesn't verify it's the git repo root. In SorraAgents, the skill is nested inside a `skill/` subdirectory, so the function returns the `skill/` subdir instead of the actual repo root (`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`).

This means:
- `REPO_ROOT` = `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`
- `SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT` = `REPO_ROOT.parent` = `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`

But sibling projects (ContextHub, etc.) live at `/home/rgardler/projects/` (parent of SorraAgents), so the scan at `SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT/*/.worklog/config.yaml` never finds them.

## Fix

Make `_resolve_repo_root()` find the actual git repo root by checking for `.git` at the found directory or its ancestors.
data.title: Fix prefix-to-sibling scan for non-framework repos
